columns.name: INFLATION_CAP
columns.comment: Needed for Index linked assets, mapped to BBG fields.

columns.name: INFLATION_FLOOR
columns.comment: Needed for Index linked assets, mapped to BBG fields.

columns.name: INFLATION_LAG
columns.comment: Number of inflation reporting periods, denoted in months, between the effective period of the inflation rate and the period in which the associated determination date occurs.         Except for Australia and New Zealand where inflation is reported on a quarterly basis and number is denoted in quarters.

columns.name: INFLATION_LINKED_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether the coupon or principal for a security is inflation linked.

columns.name: INIT_FLOATING_RATE_IDX
columns.comment: Initial stub floating rate. Normally, this is the leg floating rate i.e.  FLT_RTE_INDX, but it can be explicitly agreed

columns.name: INITIAL_PUBLIC_OFFER_DATE
columns.comment: The Date the company goes public

columns.name: INT_ACC_DATE
columns.comment: Interest Accrual Date

columns.name: INTEREST_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Code specifies if and what interest payment is generated by the security (ex. Principal Only, Interest Only, Index-Linked). Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'INTTYPE'.

columns.name: INTEREST_TYPE_DESC
columns.comment: Description specifies if and what interest payment is generated by the security (ex. Principal Only, Interest Only, Index-Linked).

columns.name: INTERNAL_SUBTYPE_CD
columns.comment: Security specific type sub-group code used to differentiate derivatives with common characteristics. This is a child group of DIM_SECURITY_DERIVATIVE.INTERNAL_TYPE_CD. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD for options where DESC_TYPE = 'FXOPTNTYPE'; for Interest Rate Caps/Floors, DESC_TYPE = 'IRCFSUBTYP'; for Repurchase Agreements, DESC_TYPE = 'REPOSUBTYP'.

columns.name: INTERNAL_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Security specific type group code used to differentiate derivatives with common characteristics.

columns.name: INTERPOLATION_FOR_COUPON_CALC
columns.comment: Interpolation method used to calculate the inflation lag for an inflation-linked bond.

columns.name: ISIN_NO
columns.comment: The ISIN number.

columns.name: ISSUE_CNTRY_CD
columns.comment: Country of issuance.

columns.name: ISSUE_CNTRY_ISO_2
columns.comment:
Two character ISO issue country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: ISSUE_CNTRY_ISO_3
columns.comment:
Three character ISO issue country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: ISSUE_CNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Country name of Issue

columns.name: ISSUE_DATE
columns.comment:
ISSUE DATE:  Date on which the security was or will be issued.
CP_ISSUE_DT: Dated date of the issue.
WRT_ISSUE_DT: The date on which the warrants are issued.
The dated date and issue date are usually the same. In those cases where interest begins accruing prior to the issue date, however, the dated date will be prior to the issue date. An example is when the dated date is a Saturday and the issue date is the following Monday.

columns.name: ISSUE_STATE_CD
columns.comment: The state where the security was issued. Code defined in DIM_STATE as STATE_CD.

columns.name: ISSUER_INDUSTRY
columns.comment: The industry classification of the issuer of the security.        For Equities, this will return the Industry Subgroup (DS202, INDUSTRY_SUBGROUP) of the issuer.

columns.name: JUNIOR_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether or not the security rank is junior.  A junior security is a security  that ranks lower than other securities in regards to the owner's claims on assets and income in the event of the issuer becoming insolvent.

columns.name: LAST_PAYMENT_DATE
columns.comment: The last payment date

columns.name: LAST_TRADEABLE_DATE
columns.comment: Last date that the contract is available for trade. Warrants: This field supported for Korea, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand covered warrants. For other markets and uncovered warrants, it will be supported when provided.

columns.name: LATEST_REVIEW_DATE
columns.comment: The most recent date on which the asset, credit, or exposure was formally reviewed.

columns.name: LEG_TYPE
columns.comment: Description of the leg - FIX,FLO, etc.

columns.name: LEGACY_ASSET_TYPE
columns.comment: Legacy LGIM Asset Type

columns.name: LGIM_ASSET_TYPE
columns.comment: LGIMAssetType

columns.name: LGIM_ASSET_TYPE_L2
columns.comment: LGIMAssetTypeL2

columns.name: LGIM_ASSET_TYPE_L3
columns.comment: LGIMAssetTypeL3

columns.name: LGIM_D_BBG_CUSTOM_L1
columns.comment: Vendor data for Barclays Sector (P.K.A LBFI_DERIVED Level 1)

columns.name: LGIM_D_BBG_CUSTOM_L2
columns.comment: Vendor data for Barclays Sector (P.K.A LBFI_DERIVED Level 2)

columns.name: LGIM_D_BBG_CUSTOM_L3
columns.comment: Vendor data for Barclays Sector (P.K.A LBFI_DERIVED Level 3)

columns.name: LGIM_D_BBG_CUSTOM_L4
columns.comment: Vendor data for Barclays Sector (P.K.A LBFI_DERIVED Level 4)

columns.name: LGIM_HIGH_YIELD
columns.comment: Security classification;  used to determine whether bond is investment grade

columns.name: LIEN_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Lien type code. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'LIENTYPCD'.

columns.name: LIQUIDITY_SCORE
columns.comment: Bloomberg Port: Liquidity Score. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT5

columns.name: LIST_EXCH_CD
columns.comment: Exchange on which security is listed. Code defined in DIM_EXCHANGE as EXCH_CD.

columns.name: LIST_EXCH_NAME
columns.comment: The listed exchange name

columns.name: LOANX_ID
columns.comment: Unique Identifier for each loan

columns.name: LOC_CRRNCY_CD
columns.comment: The pricing/settlement currency of the asset. Code defined in DIM_CURRENCY as CRRNCY_CD.

columns.name: LOT_SIZE
columns.comment: Security lot size i.e. number of trading units for non-derivative instruments.

columns.name: LOWER_TIER2_CAPITAL_IND
columns.comment: Indicates the classification of the capital adequacy of a bank. Tier 2 capital has a limited life span, thus making it less effective as a safeguard against losses by a bank. This class of capital has a minimum maturity of five years and coupon payments are not deferrable. Field is only applicable to pre-Basel III designations. For the current Basel III tier designation please see the Basel III Designation field (DZ901, BASEL_III_DESIGNATION).

columns.name: MAKE_WHOLE_CALL_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the security has a make whole call.        Munis:    A make whole call is a provision that allows a borrower to prepay the remaining fixed rate term debt. The borrower, however, has to make an additional payment that is derived from a formula based on the net present value of the future debt payments.

columns.name: MAKE_WHOLE_TERMINATION_DATE
columns.comment: Represents the first date where the make well or make whole call option is no longer available.

columns.name: MARKET_CAP
columns.comment: Market value of the company's outstanding shares at the time of the offering calculated by multiplying the shares outstanding by the offer price. This market capitalization is restricted to the security type of the offering and does not account for multiple share classes.

columns.name: MARKET_SECTOR_DES
columns.comment: Market Sector Description

columns.name: MASTER_DOC_DATE
columns.comment: Master Document Date

columns.name: MASTER_DOC_TRANS_TYPE
columns.comment: Master Document Transaction Type.

columns.name: MATURE_DATE
columns.comment: The maturity date (required for fixed income securities).

columns.name: MATURITY_IN_DAYS
columns.comment: Bloomberg PORT: Maturity in Days. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT6.

columns.name: MATURITY_TYPE
columns.comment: Specifies the redemption features of the security, Examples include at maturity, callable, puttable, sinkable and may include combinations if applicable. Maturity Type Lookup (DM002, LU_MTY_TYP) specifies the potential return values for Maturity / Refund Type.

columns.name: MIC_PRIMARY_EXCHANGE_CD
columns.comment: ISO Market Identification Code (MIC) of the Bloomberg assigned primary exchange on which this specific security is traded.         For Non-Traded Securities:     This will be blank.        For futures and options:    This field will deliver the Segment MIC (Market Identification Code) where applicable; else the Operating MIC will be returned.

columns.name: MIN_INCREMENT_INVEST_AMT
columns.comment: The minimum incremental amount of money to invest after the initial investment in the fund.

columns.name: MIN_TRADE_QTY
columns.comment:
Minimum trading unit for U.S. stocks.

The minimum amount of funds that can be allocated for a long or short position according to the trading requirements of a certain security or financial instrument.

columns.name: MKT_CAP_RELATIVE
columns.comment: Relative market cap size (e.g. small, medium, large) of an equity security

columns.name: MKT_ISSUE
columns.comment: Market in which the bonNature of what underlies or backs the liability the security represents

columns.name: MORT_CURRENT_FACE
columns.comment: The Current face refers to the  current par value of a mortgage-backed security (MBS). It reveals the remaining monthly principal on a group of home mortgages, providing investors with a snapshot of how an MBS, the vehicle collecting on these loans, is doing compared to when it started out.

columns.name: MORT_ORIGINAL_FACE
columns.comment: The face value at the issue date.

columns.name: MORTGAGE_CURRENT_PAY_DATE
columns.comment: Payment date of the current settlement month.

columns.name: MORTGAGE_DEAL_TYPE
columns.comment: Description of the type of deal. I.e. REMIC, HOME EQTY. Applies to CMO/ABS deals

columns.name: MORTGAGE_FACTOR
columns.comment: The mortgage factor.

columns.name: MORTGAGE_FACTOR_SETTLE_DATE_ACCRUAL_DATE
columns.comment: The first day of the next accrual period determined by the factor for the settle date.

columns.name: MORTGAGE_FINAL_PAY_DATE
columns.comment: Projected final payment date.

columns.name: MORTGAGE_NUMBER_BONDS_IN_DEAL
columns.comment: Number of tranches in the deal or collateral group. Applicable to CMO/ABS.

columns.name: MOST_RECENT_REPORTED_FACTOR
columns.comment: The quotient of the current amount outstanding divided by the original amount outstanding. For various inflation-linked securities: 1) if it is a sinking fund, it returns sinking factor as of the settlement date 2) if the factor has been applied into price and accrued interest, the field is reset to 1 (Swedish index-linked bonds) 3) in all other situations it returns index ratio (such as Canadian or French index-linked bonds) 4) For bonds with prices inclusive of the factor, all-in, this field will return 1. Calc 1227 is the only exception to this rule. It will return the current value of capitalized principal / original principal.

columns.name: MOST_SENIOR_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if a bond is the most senior in a structured finance transaction in accordance with European Union (EU) Directive 2009/138 (Solvency II).         For these purposes, a tranche is deemed the most senior where, after the delivery of an enforcement notice and where applicable an acceleration notice, the tranche is not subordinated to other tranches of the same securitization transaction in respect of receiving principal and interest payments, without taking into account amounts due under interest rate or currency derivative contracts, fees or other similar payments.

columns.name: MTG_RT_DUR
columns.comment: BBG field = 'MTG Rt Dur'. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT15

columns.name: MULTI_COUPON_SCHEDULE_TYPE
columns.comment: Clarifies the output of Multiple Coupon Schedule (SC011, MULTI_CPN_SCHEDULE).  SC020 will return a 0, 1, or 2. 0 will return if the issue is not a multi coupon issue. 1 will return if the MULTI_CPN_SCHEDULE is listed in percent terms. 2 will return if the MUTLI_CPN_SCHEDULE will return as an actual currency amount.

columns.name: MUNI_ISSUE_SIZE
columns.comment: Returns the aggregate of the entire deal size (in USD (United States Dollars)), comprising all the series of bonds brought to market by the same lead underwriter in the deal to which the security belongs as detailed in the official statement. If all series have a new money portion and a remarketed portion, the amounts will not be aggregated.

columns.name: MUNI_MATURITY_SIZE
columns.comment: Dollar amount of bonds issued under this maturity. For Zero Coupon Bonds the dollar amount represents the initial principal value. Reference Maturity Amount (DS949, MTY_AMT) for the final Maturity Value of Zero Coupon Bonds.

columns.name: MUNI_VARIABLE_INITIAL_COUPON_RATE
columns.comment: The first coupon rate assigned to the maturity at issuance.

columns.name: N_DAY_PERIOD
columns.comment: Returns number of days in the period when the frequency is chosen to be N Day Period. It is the difference of period end date of this period and period end date of the previous period.

columns.name: NACE_CLASS_CD
columns.comment: Class code of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_CLASS_NAME
columns.comment: Class name of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_DIVISION_CD
columns.comment: Division code of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_DIVISION_NAME
columns.comment: Division name of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_GROUP_CD
columns.comment: Group code of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_GROUP_NAME
columns.comment: Group name of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_SECTOR_CD
columns.comment: Sector code of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NACE_SECTOR_NAME
columns.comment: Sector name of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European community, commonly referred to as NACE (for the French term "nomenclature statistique des activites economiques dans la Communaute europeenne").

columns.name: NEW_SEC_CD
columns.comment: The Data Quality field in the Security Master identifies the completeness or quality of the security data. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'DATAQUAL'.  Codes reserved for system use: 0, 6-9, N-Z; Codes available for use: 1-5, A-M. Any system restricted codes should be replaced with available ones.

columns.name: NEXT_CASH_FLOW_AMT
columns.comment: The next cash flow relative to the last positive accrued interest date.

columns.name: NEXT_PAR_CALL_DATE
columns.comment: Provides the next date at which the issuer can redeem or call the bond at a price of par. For continuously callable bonds, Call Schedule - Discrete (SC004,CALL_DISCRETE=N), it is determined based on today's date and Call Notification - Minimum Days (DS909, CALL_NOTIFICATION_MIN_DAYS). When Call Notification - Minimum Days is null, 30 days is used as the default. Once the security has no potential to be called at par, the field will return null.

columns.name: NEXT_REVIEW_DATE
columns.comment: The next scheduled date for reviewing the asset, exposure or agreement.

columns.name: NEXT_SINK_DATE
columns.comment: The next date at which the issuer will satisfy the sinking fund payment.

columns.name: NON_DELIV_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether derivative contract is a non-deliverable contract (contract but not leg level designation only).

columns.name: NXT_CALL_PX
columns.comment: Next Call Price

columns.name: OAS12MCHANGE
columns.comment: BBG field = 'OAS12MChange'. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT22

columns.name: OAS1MCHANGE
columns.comment: BBG field = 'OAS1MChange'. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT19

columns.name: OAS1WCHANGE
columns.comment: BBG field = 'OAS1WChange '. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT18

columns.name: OAS3MCHANGE
columns.comment: BBG field = 'OAS3MChange'. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT20

columns.name: OAS6MCHANGE
columns.comment: BBG field = 'OAS6MChange'. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT21

columns.name: ON_THE_RUN_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether security/index in on-the-run i.e. is most recently issued.

columns.name: OPTION_CONTRACT_SIZE_REAL
columns.comment: Number of shares that can be exchanged for each option contract exercised.  The value is not rounded.

columns.name: OPTION_EXERCISE_DATE
columns.comment: Overridable field. Default value is equal to expiration date. The date when  the maximal returns for a call/put covered write are calculated. Displayed in format 'yyyymmdd' and 'mm/dd/yy'. The override must be typed in format 'yyyymmdd'.         Bloomberg Terminal:     This is a replication of the corresponding feature in the CWS<GO>/PWS<GO> function on the Bloomberg Terminal.

columns.name: OPTION_EXERCISE_TYPE
columns.comment: There are three ways an option can be exercised: American, European or Bermudan.

columns.name: OPTION_FINANCE_RATE
columns.comment: Calculated for each option series. For all equities and indices, the actual rate used is interpolated from the relevant swap curve. For all other securities, it is interpolated from the local government yield curve. For example, EURO = I13, JPY = I18 and HKD = I95. Please refer to {IYC1<Go>} to see more government curves by country. Also, for equities and indices, the rate is continuous by default.        History is available for BVAL OTC deals only.

columns.name: OPTION_FIRST_TRADE_DATE
columns.comment: The first date an option series is eligible to trade.

columns.name: OPTION_PUT_CALL_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether the security is a put or call.         Index and Equity:    This field will return either 'Call' for a call option or 'Put' for a put option.        Currency and  Commodity:    This field will return either 'C' for a call option, 'P' for a put option, 'T' for a touch option, 'F' for a forward or 'M' for a multi-leg option.    For Currency options, the call/put indicator is relative to the notional currency.

columns.name: OPTION_TICK_VAL
columns.comment: Value of the smallest incremental change allowable in the option price. Calculated as Option Tick Size (OP162) * Option Multiplier (OP149). Calculated as Option Tick Size (OP162) * Contract Size if there is no contract multiplier, as is the case for some exchanges.

columns.name: OTC_CONTRACT_DATE
columns.comment: Contract date for OTC derivative security.

columns.name: OTC_LEG_ID
columns.comment: Internal OTC Hub Leg Identifier of the security (NOT the SSC_ID)

columns.name: PAR_UNIT
columns.comment: Par value of the security for fixed income and equity securities.

columns.name: PAYMENT_RANK
columns.comment: Payment Rank Short Description

columns.name: PC_ASSET_CREDIT_ANALYST_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: Credit Analyst assoicated with internal rating.

columns.name: PC_ASSET_CREDIT_ANALYST_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: Credit Analyst assoicated with internal rating.

columns.name: PC_CALLABLE_IND
columns.comment: Private Credit: Indicates if asset is callable: Y/N

columns.name: PC_COVERED_IND
columns.comment: Private Credit: Covered indicator Y/N

columns.name: PC_EXTENDIBLE_IND
columns.comment: Private Credit: Extendible indicator Y/N

columns.name: PC_GOVT_GUARANTEE_CNTRY_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: Country of Government Guarantee

columns.name: PC_GOVT_GUARANTEE_CNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Private Credit: Country of Government Guarantee

columns.name: PC_INSTRUMENT_FORMAT_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: The format of the instrument.

columns.name: PC_INSTRUMENT_FORMAT_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: The format of the instrument.

columns.name: PC_INVESTMENT_MANAGER_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: The board owner of the asset.

columns.name: PC_INVESTMENT_MANAGER_NAME
columns.comment: Private Credit: The board owner of the asset.

columns.name: PC_MAKE_WHOLE_CALL_IND
columns.comment: Private Credit: An indicator showing if a borrower can terminate a loan prematurely.  Y/N

columns.name: PC_MATCHING_ADJUSTMENT_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: A provision under Solvency II designed to help insurers with long-term liabilities meet the solvency capital requirement. The MA is an addition to the risk-free rate used to discount annuitant liabilities and its main benefit is a significant reduction in the size of these liabilities.

columns.name: PC_OPTIONALITY_ASSET_MANAGEMENT_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: If  loan can be recalled early by the lender: with Call Exit Option (right of lender  to demand early repayment) or Put Exit Option (right of lender to require borrower to repay) or 'None' of above.Create as Dropdown: 'Optionality (Asset Management)'. Values: None, Put Option, Call Option

columns.name: PC_OPTIONALITY_ASSET_MANAGEMENT_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: If  loan can be recalled early by the lender: with Call Exit Option (right of lender  to demand early repayment) or Put Exit Option (right of lender to require borrower to repay) or 'None' of above.Create as Dropdown: 'Optionality (Asset Management)'. Values: None, Put Option, Call Option

columns.name: PC_PRICING_FREQUENCY_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: The frequency with which security is priced

columns.name: PC_PRINCIPAL_FACTOR_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: The different types of factor applied to the asset which effects the nominal value. Permitted values are Current Factor, Index Ratio, Sink Factor

columns.name: PC_PRINCIPAL_FACTOR_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: The different types of factor applied to the asset which effects the nominal value. Permitted values are Current Factor, Index Ratio, Sink Factor

columns.name: PC_REINVESTMENT_BENCHMARK_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: A market recognised index that is a component of a penalty charge to the borrower if they fail to meet the criteria of the loan agreement.

columns.name: PC_REINVESTMENT_BENCHMARK_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: A market recognised index that is a component of a penalty charge to the borrower if they fail to meet the criteria of the loan agreement.

columns.name: PC_REPAYMENT_STRUCTURE_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: The style in which the borrower will repay the principle amount of the loan.

columns.name: PC_REPAYMENT_STRUCTURE_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: The style in which the borrower will repay the principle amount of the loan.

columns.name: PC_SECTOR_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: Sector of the issuer.

columns.name: PC_SECTOR_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: Sector of the issuer.

columns.name: PC_SUBSECTOR_CD
columns.comment: Private Credit: SubSector of the issuer.

columns.name: PC_SUBSECTOR_DESC
columns.comment: Private Credit: SubSector of the issuer.

columns.name: PERCENT_SINK_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if sinking fund amounts display as a percentage of issue sinker rather than cash amounts.

columns.name: PERPETUAL_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether a bond is considered Perpetual (no maturity date).

columns.name: PIK_TOGGLE_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether PIK Toggle feature applies to the loan.

columns.name: POSITION_MULTIPLICATION_FACTOR
columns.comment: Returns a factor that, when multiplied with both the security's price and position together, calculates trade money.        Fixed Income Securities:     To calculate trade money on a fixed income security position of [$]5,000 using Position Multiplication Factor of 10 and a price of par:            Trade Money = 5 * 10 * 100  = [$]5,000        Equities:     To calculate trade money on an equity position of 1,000 shares using Position Multiplication Factor of 1 and a share price of [$]5:            Trade money = 1000 * 1 * 5 = [$]5,000

columns.name: PRCING_MULT
columns.comment: The pricing multiplier is used in the formula for calculating amount based on a given quantity of a security. It is different based on the pricing model of a particular security. For equities the pricing multiplier is 1 and for bonds it is typically 0.01. The basic formula for calculating the market value of a security is Amount = Quantity * Price * Pricing Multiplier * Contract Size.

columns.name: PRICE_FULL
columns.comment: Bloomberg Port: Price (Full). Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT70.

columns.name: PRICING_SYMBOL
columns.comment: Pricing Symbol. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR1

columns.name: PRIMARY_CNTRY_OF_LISTED_EXCH_CD
columns.comment: Provides the country that a security is listed for exchange.

columns.name: PRIN_EXCH_CD
columns.comment: Code indicating if and when the swap payments (notional amount) are made. Applies to NDS Swaps. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'PRINCEXCH'.

columns.name: PRIN_EXCH_DESC
columns.comment: Description indicating if and when the swap payments (notional amount) are made. Applies to NDS Swaps. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'PRINCEXCH'.

columns.name: PRINCIPAL_FACTOR
columns.comment: The aggregated factor of all adjustments to the principal amount as of a specific settlement date. E.g. on a capitalizing bond this would be the capitalization factor plus the accrued capitalization factor. On a sinking fund bond this value will be equal to or adjusted by the sink factor. On an index linked bond this value may be adjusted by the Index Ratio (DS272, IDX_RATIO). For bonds with prices inclusive of the factor, all-in, this field will return 1. Other types of factors can be applicable.

columns.name: PRINCIPAL_FACTOR_DESC
columns.comment: Provides the Principal Factor (DY201, PRINCIPAL_FACTOR) type. If the Principal Factor is a combination of more than one factor, then the description "Principal Factor" is returned. If only one factor is involved, then the description reflects the nature of the factor.

columns.name: PRIV_PLCMNT
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether the security is a private placement.

columns.name: PRO_RATA_SINK_IND

columns.name: SALES_REVENUE_TURNOVER
columns.comment: INDUSTRIALS    Amount of sales generated by a company after the deduction of sales returns, allowances, discounts, and sales based taxes.  Includes revenues from financial subsidiaries in industrial companies if the consolidation includes those subsidiaries throughout the report.  Includes subsidies from federal or local government in certain industries (i.e. transportation or utilities).  Excludes turnover from joint ventures and/or associates.  Excludes inter-company revenue.  Excludes revenues from discontinued operations.  Figure is reported in millions; the Scaling Format Override (DY339, SCALING_FORMAT) can be used to change the display units for the field.  Users can set their preference to return 'GAAP' (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or 'ADJUSTED' data through Fundamental Analysis Defaults.  The field FA Adjusted Financials Override (DT094, FA_ADJUSTED) can be used to return Adjusted (excluding abnormal items) data ('Y') or GAAP data ('N').        BANKS & FINANCIALS    Gross revenue from any operating activity.  Total revenue is defined as the sum of total interest income, investment income, trading profit (loss), commissions and fees earned and other operating income.  Excludes revenue from discontinued operations.  Revenue may be negative due to large trading account losses.        INSURANCES    All revenues from any operating activities.  The sum of net premiums earned, realized investment gain (loss), investment income, real estate operations, and other income.        UTILITIES    Includes revenues from electric, gas, water and other operating revenue.  All revenues from any operating activity (principal activities).  Gross revenues less adjustments.  Excludes internal or inter-company revenues, except for privately held companies (utility subsidiaries).        REITS    Revenues from real estate operating activities. Total of rental income, real estate sales (for Real Estate Operating companies), management and advisory fees, mortgage and note income and other operating income.  Excludes equity in income from unconsolidated entities.  Excludes gain/(loss) on sale of rental properties.

For Corp/Pfd, this field will return Y if one of the following is TRUE:       1. Inflation Indexed Bonds where Inflation-Linked Indicator (DS686, INFLATON_LINKED_INDICATOR) = Y        2. Securities where Pro Rata Call Indicator (DX032, PRO_RATA_CALL) = Y        3. Securities where Pro Rata Sink Indicator (DX033, PRO_RATA_SINK) = Y       4. Securities where Collateral Type (DS119, COLLAT_TYP = EQUIPMENT TRUST or PASS THRU CERTS        5. Securities where Most Recently Reported Factor (DS779, MOST_RECENT_REPORTED_FACTOR is not equal to 1.        For Mortgages, this field will automatically be updated to Y for every new security.        For Government Securities, this field will return Y for Treasury Inflation Index Linked Securities and Treasury Inflation Index Linked Strips.

columns.name: SECURITY_TYP2_DESC

Program types U.S. CD and Euro CD will both return "CD" for this field, likewise U.S. CP and Euro CP programs will return a value of "CP".        Preferred:    For securities on the preferred yellow key this field is constant and will always return a value of "PREFERRED STOCK", describing the type of security.        Government:    Returns "Bill", "Note" or "Bond" depending upon the type of U.S. government security being referenced.        Mortgages and cash structured products:    Returns type of structured product (for Residential Mortgage Backed Securities (RMBS), Commercial Mortgage Backed Securities (CMBS), and Asset Backed Securities (ABS)) or types of underlying asset (for Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLO) and Collateralized Debt Obligations (CDO)) of a Deal, Pool, or To Be Announced (TBA).

Loans:    Further defines the class of debt of a loan.        Municipals:     This returns the Coupon Type (DS086, CPN_TYP) of the bond.        Mortgages and Cash Structured products:    Further classifies the type of instrument.

columns.comment: Swap agreement specific type sub-group code used to differentiate swaps with common characteristics

columns.name: SWAP_SUB_TYPE_DESC
columns.comment: Swap agreement specific type sub-group description used to differentiate swaps with common characteristics

columns.name: SWAP_TENOR
columns.comment: Swap tenor. Time frame component of a tenor is represented by D = Day, W = Week, M = Month, or Y = Year. Examples for a single term tenors are 6D (6 days), 6W (6 weeks), 6M (6 months), and 6Y (6 years). Examples for two term tenors are 6M6Y (6 months by 6 years) and 10Y20Y (10 year by 20 year) . Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'SWAPTENOR'.

columns.name: SWAP_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Type of the swap agreement code

columns.name: SWAP_TYPE_DESC
columns.comment: Type of the swap agreement description

columns.name: TICK_SIZE
columns.comment: Identifies the minimum price movement of a trading instrument. The price movements of different trading instruments vary, with their tick sizes representing the minimum amount they can move up or down on an exchange.

columns.name: TICK_VAL
columns.comment: Value of a minimum permissible price fluctuation of a futures contract.

columns.name: TICKER
columns.comment: The ticker.

columns.name: TICKER_AND_EXCH_CD
columns.comment: Ticker Exchange Code

columns.name: TIER1_CAPITAL_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the security qualifies as Tier 1 capital in regards to the capital adequacy of a bank.     Only applicable to pre-Basel III designations. For the current Basel III tier designation please see the Basel III Designation field (DZ901, BASEL_III_DESIGNATION).

columns.name: TIER2_CAPITAL_NON_SPECIFIC_IND
columns.comment: Indicates the classification of the capital adequacy of a bank. Tier 2 capital is secondary bank capital that includes items such as undisclosed reserves, general loss reserves, and subordinated term debt. Field is only applicable to pre-Basel III designations. For the current Basel III tier designation please see the Basel III Designation field (DZ901, BASEL_III_DESIGNATION).

columns.name: TODAY_TO_MATURITY_YEARS
columns.comment: Number of years from today to maturity. This is calculated as:         Number of days from today to maturity / 365.25 (to account for leap year).        Portfolio:    Weighted average of holdings' Effective Maturity as available in the Portfolio & Risk Analytics function.        Municipals:    Number of days from today to the earlier of pre-refund date or maturity/365.25 (to account for leap year.)

columns.name: TRADE_ACCRUED_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether loan does trade with accrued interest.

columns.name: TRADING_DAY_END_TIME
columns.comment: Trading day end time for a given security in Bloomberg. Time given in the user's time zone.

columns.name: TRADING_DAY_START_TIME
columns.comment: Trading day start time for a given security in Bloomberg. The start time generally includes the continuous regular trading session for a security and excludes pre auction and post close trading activity. Time given in the user's time zone.

columns.name: TRADING_STATUS
columns.comment: Trading status of the security. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'TRDSTATUS'.

columns.name: TRADING_STATUS_DESC
columns.comment: Trading status Description of the security. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'TRDSTATUS'.

columns.name: TRANCHE
columns.comment: The tranche number.

columns.name: TRANCHE_NUMBER
columns.comment: Tranche number of the security.        Mortgages:    Collateralized mortgage obligation (CMO) tranche number assigned by the Bloomberg mortgage-backed securities (MBS) structured product modeling teams based upon the deal structures.        Corporates:    Tranche identifier assigned to a bond by the issuer or underwriter(s). For covered bonds and Islamic bonds, this indicates the tranche of a larger program.The field is sourced from bloomberg fieldDY150(TRANCHE_NUM)

columns.name: UNIT_TRADED_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the security is eligible for Unit Trade eligible.

columns.name: UNIT_TRUST_ACCT_CD
columns.comment:
An unincorporated mutual fund structure that allows funds to hold assets and pass through profits to the individual owners, rather than reinvest profits back into the fund.
This is the account code. Code defined in DIM_ACCOUNT as ACCT_CD.

columns.name: UNSECURED_IND
columns.comment: Indicates the obligation is not backed by any collateral.

columns.name: UNSUBORDINATED_IND
columns.comment: Indicates a security that does not rank lower in priority than other securities when dividends are paid or assets are distributed in liquidation or bankruptcy.

columns.name: UPPER_TIER2_CAPITAL_IND
columns.comment: Indicates the classification of the capital adequacy of a bank. Also referred to as 'hybrid bonds', this type of debt is classified as Tier 2 capital with no fixed maturity date (also known as perpetual), and actually resembles Tier 1 capital. The only difference between Upper Tier 2 and Tier 1 is that the coupon payments in Upper Tier 2 are cumulative. Both Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital securities have deferrable interest, however the only difference is Tier 2 capital securities must pay cumulatively and Tier 1 can be deferred without cumulative payment. Field is only applicable to pre-Basel III designations. For the current Basel III tier designation please see the Basel III Designation field (DZ901, BASEL_III_DESIGNATION).

columns.name: USE_OF_PROCEEDS
columns.comment: Use of Proceeds

columns.name: VOLUME_AVG_20D
columns.comment: Number of shares traded on average for the past 20 trading days

columns.name: VOLUME_AVG_3M
columns.comment: Number of shares traded on average for the past three trading months.

columns.name: VOTING_RIGHTS
columns.comment: Voting Rights Per Share

columns.name: WARRANT_SETTLE_TYPE
columns.comment: The type of settlement for the warrant: cash, physical, or cash/physical.

columns.name: YANKEE_EURO
columns.comment: Code designating bonds considering their country of issuance and denomination currency (ex. Yankee, Euro). Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'YANKEEEURO'.

columns.name: ZERO_COUPON_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the bond is a zero coupon bond

columns.name: SEC_ID
columns.comment: Identifier of the security.

columns.name: SERVICE_CD
columns.comment: The service code. Different services are defined per provider.

columns.name: AS_OF_DATE
columns.comment: Business Date of Data Snapshot

columns.name: ACCRUAL_DAYS
columns.comment: The numbers of days required to accrue/accumulate  interest amount.

columns.name: ANNUAL_CONVEXITY
columns.comment: Annual convexity

columns.name: ANNUAL_MOD_DURATION
columns.comment: Annual modified duration

columns.name: ANNUAL_YTM
columns.comment: Annual yield to maturity

columns.name: AVG_BID_ASK_SPREAD_PERCENT
columns.comment: Average of all bid/ask spreads taken as a percentage of the mid price. The bid/ask points used for the computation correspond to the quotes received for the period indicated by Calc Interval (PX393, CALC_INTERVAL) (default value is five days) ending in the complete trading day prior to the date indicated by End Date Override (PX392, END_DATE_OVERRIDE) (default value is latest completed trading day). For a trading day to contribute to the calculation, there should be at least ten valid bid/ask spread points on that day. The field returns values only if more than 50% of trading days in the period are eligible to contribute to the calculation. The Calc Interval (PX393, CALC_INTERVAL) override will only support periods from one day (1D) up to 30 days (30D).

columns.name: AVG_DAILY_VAL_TRADED_6M
columns.comment: The average daily value traded for the past 6 trading months.

columns.name: AVG_LIFE
columns.comment: The weighted average time in years to receipt of future principal payments.

columns.name: AVG_VOL_10D
columns.comment: Number of shares traded on average for the past 10 trading days. The average is calculated based on the total volume over the last 10 trading days divided by 10. The end date for past 10 days is always the prior business day.        Fixed Income:    If there is no volume from the prior business day, the end date will be the most recent date that has volume within the past 10 days.  In such cases, the number of trading days used in the calculation could be less than 10.

columns.name: AVG_VOL_30D
columns.comment: Number of shares traded on average for the past 30 trading days. The average is calculated based on the total volume over the last 30 trading days divided by 30. The end date for past 30 days is always the prior business day.        Equity and Index Futures    Volume traded on average for the past 200 business days using only days that have volume, up to 30 days worth of data. If less than 30 days, it will use all the available data points for the average.        Fixed Income:     If there is no volume from the prior business day, the end date will be the most recent date that has volume within the past 30 days. In such cases, the number of trading days used in the calculation could be less than 30. Days with zero volume are included in the average calculation.

columns.name: BASIC_SPREAD
columns.comment: Basic Spread (Percent)

columns.name: BETA
columns.comment: Beta - measure of stock's volatility

columns.name: BETA_RAW_OVERRIDABLE
columns.comment: Raw (historical) beta measures the volatility of the stock price relative to the volatility in the market index. Beta is the percent change in the price of the stock given a 1% change in the market index. This field requires a minimum of 3 data points for it to work. Bloomberg Terminal & API: This is calculated from the overrides in fields Beta Start Date Override (RK390, BETA_OVERRIDE_START_DT), Beta End Date Override (RK391, BETA_OVERRIDE_END_DT), Beta Relative Index Override (RK392, BETA_OVERRIDE_REL_INDEX) and Beta Periodicity Override (RK393, BETA_OVERRIDE_PERIOD).

columns.name: BETA_RELATIVE_INDEX_OVERRIDE
columns.comment: The relative index override for calculation of customizable beta fields. This field is used for overrides only; the field, along with RK390, RK391 and RK393, is used to customize beta calculation, which affects fields RK394 through RK402.

columns.name: BID_CALCULATED_G_SPREAD
columns.comment: Calculated bid spread between the bond and the interpolated yield of the government curve. It is given in basis points.

columns.name: BID_CALCULATED_I_SPREAD
columns.comment: Calculated bid spread between the bond and the interpolated yield of the swap curve. It is given in basis points.

columns.name: BID_CONVEXITY
columns.comment: Rate change in duration of a bond as the bid yield changes.           Mortgages:      Uses static prepayment when shifting interest to calculate the convexity. To retrieve effective convexity, use Mtge Bid Effective Convexity (RK072, MTG_EFF_CNVX_BID).

columns.name: BID_CURRENT_YIELD
columns.comment: The yield arrived at by dividing the coupon by the current price. (Bid)

columns.name: BID_LIBOR_SWAP_SPREAD
columns.comment: The difference in basis points between the bond's yield based on its BID price and the LIBOR/Swap rate.  Will only calculate for issues with less then two years left to its maturity date.

columns.name: BID_MOD_DURATION
columns.comment: Modified Duration for Non-Mortgages based on the Bid Price (PR002, PX_BID) of the security is returned. Modified Duration for Mortgages: Uses static prepayment when shifting interest to calculate the duration. To retrieve effective duration, use Mtge Bid Effective Mod Duration (RK070, MTG_EFF_DUR_BID).

columns.name: BID_OAS_CONVEXITY
columns.comment: Rate of change in OAS duration as the bid yield changes. Data License: Field will not return data in a Data License Per Security request for bonds with a Calculation Type (DS138, CALC_TYP) of 1010. This is due to the field slowing down processing time.

columns.name: BID_OAS_EFFECTIVE_DURATION
columns.comment: Bid OAS (Option Adjusted Spread) Effective Duration for Mortgages: Measures the security's price/yield sensitivity calculated by shifting the entire yield curve, based on bid prices.

columns.name: BID_OAS_SPREAD
columns.comment: Number of basis points the spot curve would have to shift for the present value of the cash flows to equal the security's price, using the bid price.

columns.name: BID_SPREAD_TO_TREASURY
columns.comment: The spread to treasury between the conventional bid yield and the bond's currency-matched yield curve. For Brady Bonds the field returns the spread to treasury between the blended yield and the US Treasury curve. The maturity date is used to calculate the yield on the Brady bonds. This field is available historically for Brady Bonds only.

columns.name: BID_WORKOUT_DATE
columns.comment: Date that the bond is being priced to (Bid). For bullet bonds, the workout date never changes. For bonds with early redemption features, workout date will be the 'worst' date. Worst date is the corresponding date of minimum yield for callable bonds, maximum yield for puttable bonds, and maturity date for sinking funds.        This field will be blank if price to yield calculation isn't supported for the bond.        For Fixed Income:    To override this field, Bid Workout Price (DS029, WORKOUT_PX_BID) must also be overwritten.

columns.name: BID_YIELD_SPREAD_TO_BENCHMARK
columns.comment: The bid yield spread to worst to the benchmark bond. This field will not populate unless the current pricing source delivers spreads.

columns.name: BID_YTM
columns.comment: The yield of a bond calculated to maturity (Bid)

columns.name: BREAKEVEN_INFLATION
columns.comment: The difference between linearly interpolated YTM for benchmark and real YTM on an inflation-linked security.

columns.name: CMPD_FREQ_CD
columns.comment: Compounding Frequency Code

columns.name: CMPD_FREQ_DESC
columns.comment: Compounding Frequency Description

columns.name: CONVERSION_FACTOR
columns.comment: A conversion factor that can be used by compliance as a multiplier for the bucket value.

columns.name: CONVEXITY
columns.comment: The convexity -- the slope of the price-yield curve.

columns.name: CONVEXITY_TO_WORST
columns.comment: Convexity that corresponds to a bond’s effective date. This date is determined by the EFFDT classification.

columns.name: COUPON_BD_ADJ
columns.comment: Code indicating the type of the date adjustment affecting the coupon payment date relative to the corresponding Holiday/Business Day Calendar. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'DAYADJCONV'.

columns.name: COUPON_EOM_FLAG
columns.comment: Code specifying whether Floating Rate Note (FRN) coupon dates track the end-of-month dates. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'RESET_EOM'.

columns.name: COUPON_PAYMENT_AMT
columns.comment: The coupon payment amount.

columns.name: CREDIT_SPREAD_DUR
columns.comment: The credit spread duration is the sensitivity of the price of a security to changes in its credit spread.

columns.name: DELTA
columns.comment: Also known as the "Hedge Ratio", this percentage number expresses the ratio of the change in price of an option to the change in price of the underlying asset. For example, for a call option on a stock, a delta of 0.50 (or 50%) means that for every [$]1.00 that the stock moves, the option price moves by [$]0.50 or 50% of the stocks move. This field uses the 'best price' for calculation. The 'best price' is the last trade if it is between the bid price and the ask price. The 'best price is the bid price if the last trade is lower than the bid price. The 'best price' is the ask price if the last trade is higher than the ask price. If there was no trade on the current day then the bid price is used. If there was no trade and no bid then the ask becomes the 'best price'. European Options: Value is derived from the Black-Scholes formula. American Options: Value is derived numerically using a finite-difference PDE (partial differential equation) price employing a constant volatility to option maturity and a term structure of interest rates. No historical values available for exchange traded options. History is available for BVAL OTC deals only.

columns.name: DISC_MARGIN
columns.comment: Discount margin for floaters

columns.name: DURATION
columns.comment: The Macaulay duration is the weighted average term to maturity of the cash flows from a bond. Ex. 15.38

columns.name: DURATION_MAC_MID_EOD
columns.comment: End of Day Mid Macaulay Duration

columns.name: DURATION_TIME_SPREAD
columns.comment: Spread Duration times OAS (bond) or Pricing Spread (CDS)

columns.name: DURATION_TO_WORST
columns.comment: Duration that corresponds to a bond’s effective date. This date is determined by the EFFDT classification.

columns.name: DV01
columns.comment: Change in swap fair value of with a one BP shift up in the default probability curve

columns.name: EFF_SPREAD_DUR
columns.comment: Effective spread duration

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_CONVEXITY
columns.comment: Specifies the average option-adjusted convexity of constituents weighted by market value. This field is for Intercontinental Exchange Bank of America (ICE BofA).

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_DATE
columns.comment: Date a bond is priced when used in price to yield calculations.  The date is also associated with INDUST_CLASS_CD = EFFDT (Analytics - Effective Date Method).

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_DURATION
columns.comment:
Macaulay's duration is the average life of the bond measured in years. Macaulay's duration can also be thought
 of as the half life of a bond.

columns.name: EQUITY_RAW_BETA
columns.comment: Volatility measure of the percentage price change of the security given a one percent change in a representative market index. The beta value is determined by comparing the price movements of the security and the representative market index for the past two years of weekly data.        Portfolio:    Raw Beta as computed in the Portfolio & Risk Analytics function. It is measured by the slope of the regression line of the portfolio and declared benchmark daily returns over one year.

columns.name: EQY_ALPHA
columns.comment: Alpha

columns.name: EQY_DVD_YLD_IND
columns.comment: The most recently announced gross dividend, annualized based on the Dividend Frequency (DV016, DVD_FREQ), then divided by the current market price. If the security is paying an interim/final dividend, then the indicated yield is calculated by adding the gross amount from the most recently announced interim and the most recently announced final, and dividing the sum by the current market price. Abnormal Dividends are not included in this yield calculation.        The first 'true' statement about current market price in the following is used to calculate the yield:    If Last Price (PR005, PX_LAST) is available, and Bid Price (PR002, PX_BID) is greater than Last Price then use Bid Price.    If Last Price is available, and Ask Price (PR004, PX_ASK) is less than Last Price, then use Ask Price (assuming Ask Price is available)    If Last Price is available, then use Last Price     If Ask Price is available, then use Ask Price    If Bid Price is available, then use Bid Price.

columns.name: FWD_CPN_INT
columns.comment: For sell buy-back agreements, the interest earned on the sum of the underlying securities coupon cashflows paid during this security's lifetime.

columns.name: I_SPREAD
columns.comment: The interpolated spread of a bond is the difference between its yield to maturity and the linearly interpolated yield for the same maturity on an appropriate reference yield curve.

columns.name: INFLATION_DURATION
columns.comment: The second order price sensitivity to a shift in inflation rates.

columns.name: INFLATION_INDEX_RATIO
columns.comment: The inflation factor (inflation index ratio) for the security.

columns.name: INTEREST_PCT
columns.comment: The percentage of accrued interest on a fixed income security as of the current date. For example, on a bond that pays 6% annually, two months after the coupon payment date, this field should contain roughly 1.00%.

columns.name: ISSUE_BENCHMARK_SPREAD
columns.comment: Yield spread in basis points, at issuance, to the pricing benchmark. Field is also applicable for collateralized mortgage obligations (CMO)/asset backed securities (ABS) and municipal bonds.        Municipals:    Field returns spread to worst at issuance as reported by the underwriter for taxable bonds. If no return is available, underwriter did not report.

columns.name: LAST_COUPON_PERIOD_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Code describing whether the last coupon period was odd (ex. Short, Long)  or Normal.

columns.name: LQA_LIQUIDITY_SCORE
columns.comment: Measured on a scale of 1 to 100 (100 being the most liquid) that summarizes the relative liquidity of an instrument in the covered universe.  Liquidity in this sense is the ability to sell a security at the lowest cost for a comparable range of volumes.         This field is available as a premium product via Excel API and the Bloomberg BLPAPI. For more information about accessing LQA analytics, please contact your Bloomberg sales representative.

columns.name: MAKE_WHOLE_CALL_SPREAD
columns.comment: Number of basis points (if any) added to the yield on the benchmark listed, used to calculate the present value of the make-whole call premium on the bond.

columns.name: MATURITY_IN_DAYS
columns.comment: Bloomberg PORT: Maturity in Days. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_NUM.UDF_FLOAT6.

columns.name: MID_MOD_DURATION_TO_MATURITY
columns.comment: Modified duration-to-maturity based on mid price.

columns.name: MOD_DURATION
columns.comment: The modified duration.

columns.name: MOD_DURATION_TO_WORST
columns.comment: Modified Duration that corresponds to a bond’s effective date. This date is determined by the EFFDT classification.

columns.name: NEXT_CASH_FLOW_DATE
columns.comment: Date of the next cash flow relative to the last positive accrued interest date.

columns.name: NEXT_COUPON_DATE
columns.comment: The next coupon payment date.

columns.name: NEXT_RESET_DATE
columns.comment: The date which the next coupon resets.

columns.name: OAS_SWAP
columns.comment:
Flat spread which must be added to the swap curve in a pricing model (which accounts for embedded options) 
to discount a bond payment to match its market price.

columns.name: OPTION_ADJ_SPREAD
columns.comment: The Option Adjusted Spread (OAS) in basis point. It specifies the average option-adjusted spread of constituents weighted by market value.

columns.name: OPTION_ADJ_SPREAD_TO_SWAPS
columns.comment: Option Adjusted Spread (OAS) over the swap curve measured in basis points.

columns.name: OPTION_ADJ_SPREAD_TO_TSY
columns.comment: The Option Adjusted Spread (OAS) over the treasury curve measured in basis points.

columns.name: OPTN_EXPIRE_TYPE
columns.comment: Option expiration type (ex. American, European, Bermudan). Required for swaptions.

columns.name: ORG_WEIGHTED_AVG_MATURITY
columns.comment: Original Weighted Average Maturity for a pool of mortgages within a mortgage backed security

columns.name: PAR_SPREAD
columns.comment: Computed premium rate that would lead to a computed value of zero for the instrument

columns.name: PAYMENT_FREQ_CD
columns.comment: Payment frequency code

columns.name: PAYMENT_FREQ_DESC
columns.comment: Coupon Payment Frequency Description

columns.name: PREMIUM_VAL
columns.comment: Computed present value of the stream of premium payments

columns.name: PREPAY_CAP
columns.comment: The prepayment rate cap.

columns.name: PREPAY_DURATION
columns.comment:
It measures how much the bond's price can be expected to change given a change in the multiple of the 
prepayment model.

columns.name: PREPAY_FLOOR
columns.comment: The prepayment rate floor.

columns.name: PREPAY_RATE
columns.comment: The current prepayment rate assumption. Numeric value corresponds to the prepayment model defined by CALC_MODEL field (e.g. model dependent on the CPR (Constant Prepayment Rate) where value of PREPAY_RATE sets the speed of prepayments.

columns.name: PREPAY_SENSITIVE
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether the security is prepayment sensitive.

columns.name: PREV_PAYMENT_DATE
columns.comment: The previous coupon payment date (required for irregular payment securities).

columns.name: PRICE_EARNS_RATIO
columns.comment: The price to earning ratio (P/E), the price of a stock divided by its earnings per share.

columns.name: PRVDR_ID
columns.comment: The ID associated with theProvider. This provides the user with the ability to track source specific data.

columns.name: REDEMPTION_YIELD
columns.comment: Price yield for the Call, Put or Sinking Fund record

columns.name: REFERENCE_INDEX_ISDA
columns.comment: Name of the index used by inflation linked bond (ILB) / Index rate code for variable rate securities

columns.name: REL_INDEX
columns.comment: Relative Index

columns.name: RESET_IDX
columns.comment: The benchmark index used as a base rate to calculate interest.

columns.name: RESET_LAG_DAYS
columns.comment: The FRN reset lag days, the number of days to go back in the index price history to get the reset rate for today.

columns.name: RESET_LOOKBACK_DAYS
columns.comment: Days of the backward shifted observation period for compounding averaging used to determine reset rates.

columns.name: RESET_OBSERVATION_DAYS
columns.comment: The number of business days in the observation period to calculate the RFR for an interest period

columns.name: RISK_MID
columns.comment: Mid Risk

columns.name: SEMI_ANNUAL_CONVEXITY
columns.comment: The convexity -- the slope of the price-yield curve, calculated on a semi annual basis

columns.name: SEMI_ANNUAL_MOD_DURATION
columns.comment: The modified duration to maturity, calculated on a semi annual basis

columns.name: SEMI_ANNUAL_YTM
columns.comment: The yield to maturity, calculated on a semi annual basis

columns.name: SINK_FACTOR
columns.comment: The factor resulting from sinking fund provisions.

columns.name: SINK_SCHEDULE_AMT_TYPE
columns.comment: Sink Schedule Amount Type

columns.name: SPREAD
columns.comment: For Debt: Benchmark Spread, For Credit Default Swap: Deal Spread

columns.name: SPREAD_DUR
columns.comment:
Spread duration is the sensitivity of the price of a security to changes in its credit spread. The credit spread is the
 difference between the yield of a security and the yield of a benchmark rate, such as a cash interest rate or government bond yield.

columns.name: SPREAD_TO_WORST
columns.comment: The difference between the yield-to-worst of a bond and the yield-to-worst of a US Treasury security with similar duration

columns.name: SWAP_PAY_SPREAD
columns.comment: The number of basis points over/under the floating rate index that the floating rate payer is obligated to pay.

columns.name: VEGA
columns.comment: The measure of how much an option's price changes for an incremental change - usually 1% - in volatility.

columns.name: VLTLTY
columns.comment: It is measured by the day-to-day percentage difference in the price of the commodity.

columns.name: VOLATILITY_60D
columns.comment: A measure of the risk of price moves for a security calculated from the standard deviation of day to day logarithmic historical price changes. The 60-day price volatility equals the annualized standard deviation of the relative price change for the 60 most recent trading days closing price, expressed as a percentage.        Currencies:    Non-CDS (Credit Default Swap) currency securities are not supported for historical data.

columns.name: VRDN_FREQ_CD
columns.comment: Reset frequency for variable-rate securities code

columns.name: VRDN_FREQ_DESC
columns.comment: Reset frequency for variable-rate securities desc

columns.name: WAC
columns.comment: The weighted average coupon, the average coupon of all individual mortgages.

columns.name: WAM
columns.comment: The weighted average maturity, the average of all the remaining maturities of the mortgages that compose the pool.

columns.name: YAS_WORKOUT_DATE
columns.comment: Workout date for the yield provided in YAS Bond Yield (SP111, YAS_BOND_YLD).  Must be overridden with YAS Workout Price (SP149, YAS_WORKOUT_PX).

columns.name: YAS_Z_SPREAD
columns.comment: Returns the ZSpread based upon the field YAS Bond Price (SP110, YAS_BOND_PX).

columns.name: YIELD
columns.comment: Annual dividend yield (annual dividend per share divided by the price per share) expressed as a percentage.

columns.name: YIELD_TO_MAT_MID_EOD
columns.comment: End of Day Mid Yield to Maturity

columns.name: YIELD_TO_MATURE
columns.comment: The yield to maturity.

columns.name: YIELD_TO_NEXT_CALL
columns.comment: For bonds, yield assuming redemption at strike at the next call date. If the bond has no calls, it will equal Yield to Maturity.

columns.name: YIELD_TO_WORST_CALL
columns.comment: The yield to worst call.

columns.name: YTM
columns.comment: Internal rate of return earned by holding a bond bought at the market price to maturity, and assuming that all coupon and principal payments will be made on schedule. Yield to maturity is simply the discount rate at which the sum of all future cash flows from the bond (coupons and principal) is equal to the price of the bond.

columns.name: YTW
columns.comment: Lowest yield of the yield to maturity, yield to call, or yield to refunding.

columns.name: Z_SPREAD
columns.comment: The Z spread is the constant spread that makes the price of a security equal to the present value of its cash flows when added to the yield at each point on the spot rate Treasury curve where cash flow is received.

columns.name: PAYMENT_ID
columns.comment: The unique index sequence number of the payment.

columns.name: SERVICE_CD
columns.comment: The service code is a descriptive code corresponding to SERVICE_ID. Different services are defined per provider. Code defined in DIM_PROVIDER_SERVICE.

columns.name: AS_OF_DATE
columns.comment: As of Date

columns.name: PROJECTION_PAYMENT_TYPE

PRIIPs Risk Narrative - Element C

A boolean indicator of whether or not a share class is subject to currency risk:

// 7. For the purposes of the SRI presentation [...] the following narrative explanations shall be used, as appropriate:

[[Where applicable]: Element C, in bold] Be aware of currency risk. You will receive payments in a different currency, so the final return you will get depend on the exchange rate between the two currencies. This risk is not considered in the indicator shown above.

columns.name: LUXEMBOURG_TAXE_DABONNEMENT
columns.comment:
[Open Funds] Tax rate of Luxembourg taxe d'abonnement, a registration fee established on the negotiability of securities issued by Undertakings for Collective Investment (UCI), Specialised Investment Funds (SIF), Reserved Alternative Investment Funds (RAIF), and Family Wealth Management Companies (sociétés de gestion de patrimoine familial - SPF). The declaration and payment of the tax must be made each quarter._x000D_
_x000D_
Funds meeting the following conditions are exempt from this tax:_x000D_
- Shares/units of the fund must be available exclusively to institutional investors (1). If a fund has several share/unit classes, the exemption will be available only to classes the shares/units of which are available exclusively to institutional investors. _x000D_
- The exclusive investment objective of the fund must be investment in money market instruments and the placing of deposits with credit institutions;_x000D_
- The weighted residual maturity of the fund’s portfolio must not exceed 90 days; and_x000D_
- The fund must have received the highest rating from a recognized rating agency. _x000D_
_x000D_
(1) Institutional investors for this purpose include financial professionals (including banks, insurance companies, investment funds, pension funds, local authorities, industrial and financial groups) acting for their own account, and financial professionals investing in their own name but on behalf of others, subject to the investments being made pursuant to a discretionary asset management mandate and the client of the financial professional not having any right or claim directly against the fund. High net worth individuals are not institutional investors. _x000D_
_x000D_
More information may be found at https://guichet.public.lu/en/entreprises/sectoriel/organisme-placement-collectif/taxe-abonnement.html

columns.name: SRI
columns.comment: Summary Risk Indicator (SRI) is a standardized risk indicator under PRIIPS regulation that considers both the volatility of a financial instrument (market risk) and the creditworthiness of the issuer (credit risk). It is displayed as a number between 1 and 7, representing the combined risk of the product.

columns.name: SRRI_RECORD_DATE
columns.comment: [Open Funds] The Synthetic Risk and Reward Indicator (SRRI) demonstrates where the Fund ranks in terms of its potential risk and reward. The higher the rank the greater the potential reward but the greater the risk of losing money. It is not guaranteed to remain the same and may change over time. It is based on historical data and may not be a reliable indication of the future risk profile of the Fund. The methodology for the synthetic risk and reward indicator applies to all UCITS. It should be based on the volatility of the fund using weekly or monthly returns covering the previous five years. In light of the outcome of the volatility calculation, the UCITS should be assigned to the appropriate category on a numerical scale of 1 to 7

columns.name: SRRI_VAL
columns.comment:
The Synthetic Risk and Reward Indicator (SRRI) demonstrates where the Fund ranks in terms of its potential risk and reward. The higher the rank the greater the potential reward but the greater the risk of losing money. It is not guaranteed to remain the same and may change over time. It is based on historical data and may not be a reliable indication of the future risk profile of the Fund. The methodology for the synthetic risk and reward indicator applies to all UCITS. It should be based on the volatility of the fund using weekly or monthly returns covering the previous five years. In light of the outcome of the volatility calculation, the UCITS should be assigned to the appropriate category on a numerical scale of 1 to 7.

More details about the indicator and its computation methodology can be obtained under https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/guidelines-methodology-calculation-synthetic-risk-and-reward-indicator-in-key-investor
