columns.name: MAXIMAL_NUMBER_OF_POSSIBLE_DECIMALS_NAV_VAL
columns.comment: Maximal number of decimals used for NAV calculations, assuming that this figure is equal for all kind of NAVs calculated for this specific share class, e.g. valuation price, transaction price (single pricing) or bid and ask price with dual priced share classes.

columns.name: MAXIMUM_REDEMPTION_AS_PERCENTAGE_OF_NAV
columns.comment: Investors will typically be limited in the maximum percentage of the Fund they can redeem before a liquidity management tool is implemented. This is to help protect the Fund's liquidity. E.g. an investor can only redeem a maximum 10% of the Funds NAV before gating etc.

columns.name: MEMBER_COMM_PRICE_SERIES
columns.comment: Hierarchal approach where the Price series used will be the Daily Close (if available and accessible by policyholders), otherwise Daily Midday (if available and accessible by policyholders), otherwise Weekly Close

columns.name: MEMBER_COMM_REPORTING_BASIS_VAL
columns.comment: Indicates whether the Member Comms use a gross or net of fees performance return

columns.name: MEMBER_COMM_TARGET_MARKET_DESC

columns.name: MFN_STRATEGY_IND
columns.comment: If yes, this strategy has an active MFN. Most Favoured Nation.

columns.name: MIFID_GER_PRODUCT_CATEGORY_OR_NATURE_VAL
columns.comment:
Classification of products regarding the knowledge and/or experience assessment of distributors.

The translation of each code value is as follows:
01 - Shares
02 - Alternative Investment Fund - fund like UCITS with a physical commodity component
03 - Alternative Investment funds - closed-end funds / closed-end investment funds
04 - Alternative Investment Funds - Open-ended Real Estate Funds
05 - Alternative Investment Funds - Single Hedge Funds
06 - Alternative investment funds - fund of hedge funds
07 - Bonds (unstructured)
08 - Bonds with additional rights / special collateralisation
09 - Bonds with warrants
10 - Additional Tier1 bonds
11 - Profit-sharing rights
12 - Leverage products (factor certificates and ETFs with leverage >1 as per loss reporting, warrants, knock-outs)
13 - UCITS Investment funds (unstructured)
14 - Mining shares
15 - Non-linear CLNs
16 - Reverse products (certificates and ETFs)
17 - Structured investment products (certificates, structured bonds, ETCs)
18 - Structured UCITS and alternative investment funds
19 - Swap-based UCITS and alternative investment funds
20 - Worst-of-certificates
21 - Certificates with Delta 1-depiction of known financial indices
22 - Ancillary rights
24 - Contingent convertibles - bond funds (investment focus AT1)
25 - Tier2 bonds
26 - Senior non-preferred bonds
27 - Alternative investment funds - mixed and other investment funds
28 - Real Estate Investment Trust (REITs)
29 - Miscellaneous
30 - European Long Term Investment Funds (ELTIFs)

// The correspondent MiFID II field introduced by the European Working Group with their MiFID Data Dictionary Template (EMT) is:
EMT: 00090_Product_Category_or_Nature_Germany. This is a Conditional EMT field.//

columns.name: MIN_HOLDING_PERIOD_DESC
columns.comment: Describes the recommended holding period as appears on factsheets and in KIDs.  Typically 5 years except i) Cash/Money Market Funds (typically no minimum), ii) Real Assets Funds (typically no disclosure on factsheets, but disclosure in KIDs) and iii) where it mirrors the wrap of the underlying.

columns.name: MIN_PERCENTAGE_OF_INVESTMENTS_USED_TO_ATTAIN_ES_CHARACTERISTICS

columns.name: MINIMUM_PERCENTAGE_INVESTED_IN_ENVIRONMENTALLY_SUSTAINABLE_INVESTMENTS_VAL
columns.comment: Minimum percentage of the portfolio invested in environmentally sustainable investments

columns.name: MINIMUM_PERCENTAGE_INVESTED_IN_SUSTAINABLE_INVESTMENTS_WITH_SOCIAL_OBJECTIVE_VAL

columns.name: MINIMUM_SUBSCRIPTION_AMT
columns.comment: The minimum amount that clients are required to invest. Private market Funds typically have large minimum subscription amount

columns.name: MULTIPLE_CLOSES

columns.name: ON_FUND_CHARGE_OFC_RATE
columns.comment: On fund charges (OFC) include expenses associated with the fund set-up and ongoing maintenance our funds. Applicable expenses will vary across our fund ranges. On fund charges can include and are not limited to: fund administration, depositary, custody, registration, benchmark license costs, market data and professional fees.

columns.name: ON_FUND_CHARGE_OFC_RATE_EFFECTIVE_DATE
columns.comment: Effective date of On Fund Charge (OFC) Rate.

columns.name: OPERATING_EXPENSE
columns.comment: The total operating expense for the Fund expressed as a percentage.

columns.name: OTHER_REVIEW_RELATED_TO_VALUE_ANDOR_CHARGES_UK_VAL
columns.comment:
Other review related to value and or charges, either:
A – In line with ESMA supervisory briefing on the supervision of costs in UCITS and AIFs or relevant NCA supervisory activity
O – Other local requirements or procedures
Only used if OFEM090400 EMT Is Assessment of Value Required Under COLL UK is set to "no" and OFEM090600 EMT Outcome of PRIN Value Assessment or Review UK is empty. Out of scope firms may answer this field on a voluntary basis.

// The correspondent MiFID II field introduced by the European Working Group with their MiFID Data Dictionary Template (EMT) is:
EMT: 09070_Other_Review_Related_To_Value_And_Or_Charges_UK. This is an Optional EMT field.//

columns.name: OTHER_SPECIFIC_INVESTMENT_NEEDS_VAL
columns.comment:
Is the fund designed to meet other specific investment needs such as Islamic banking or other? If the fund does not meet any specific investment needs, please indicate "no".
The following list describes each meaning of the available alphanum values:
N = No
I = Islamic banking
O = Other

columns.name: OUTCOME_OF_PRIN_VALUE_ASSESSMENT_VAL
columns.comment:
Outome of PRIN value assessment or review, either:
1 – product expected to provide fair value for reasonably foreseeable period
2 – review indicates significant changes required in order to provide fair value
Only used if OFEM090500 EMT Outcome of COLL Assessment of Value UK is set to "no". Note PRIN 2A.4.2R, PRIN 2A.4.5R, and PRIN 2A.4.16R. Out of scope firms may answer this field on a voluntary basis.

EMT: 09060_Outcome_Of_PRIN_Value_Assessment_Or_Review_UK. This is a Conditional EMT field.//

columns.name: OWNER_TEAM_NAME
columns.comment: Team who is responsible within LGIM

columns.name: PAIF_IND
columns.comment: This field is only relevant for UK based funds. If this is not the case, please leave the field empty. Is the fund a Property Authorised Investment Fund (PAIF)? A PAIF is an authorised investment fund primarily invested in property and is a UK regulated fund vehicle. There is no taxation of property profits at fund level. Only eligible investors (e.g. Individual Savings Account, Self Invested Personal Pension) are allowed to invest in PAIF.

columns.name: PARENT_FUND_CD
columns.comment: An identifier used to group funds with similar characteristics.  A “parent” fund is the ‘main’ version of the fund with other funds being ‘iterations’ of it.  Typically the parent fund code is a SCOPE ID of the ‘main’ version of the fund, but alternatively it may be text that describes ‘batches’ of similar funds where it is not appropriate to have a single code as parent e.g. “Single Stock Gilts”

columns.name: PARENT_GROUP_NAME
columns.comment: The main fund name associated with the Parent Fund Code. Typically the heading under which funds are grouped in PMC literatrure

columns.name: PARENT_SUBORDINATE
columns.comment: Used to help define groups funds with similar characteristics.  A “parent” fund is the ‘main’ version of the fund with other funds being ‘iterations’ of it.  Iterations are classified as "sub-ordinate funds".

columns.name: PASSIVE_FUND_IND
columns.comment: Does the fund follow an index very closely?

columns.name: PASSIVE_INVESTMENT_STYLE
columns.comment: This field is exclusively for passive strategies and it defines how the PMs are managing relative to the benchmark.

columns.name: PAY_DATE
columns.comment: The date on which Income is paid in a respective Fund

columns.name: PERFORMANCE_BENCHMARK_TAX_CAVEAT
columns.comment: A statement required for factsheets with regards to the tax status of the benchmark being used vs the tax treatment of the fund

columns.name: PERFORMANCE_FEE
columns.comment: For PMC Funds this is the performance fee levied by PMC, for PMC wrapped funds it does not take into account any exit charge levied by the underlying fund.

columns.name: PRICE_TYPE
columns.comment: Details the type of pricing used by the Fund.

columns.name: PRICING_METHODOLOGY
columns.comment:
In general there are "Dual Pricing Funds" and "Single Pricing Funds"._x000D_
_x000D_
The value "dual pricing" refers to a fund, which calculates two NAVs, firstly the so-called "offer price", a NAV for subscribers derived from underlying security offer prices and secondly the so-called "bid price", a NAV for redeemers, derived from underlying security bid prices._x000D_
_x000D_
A "single pricing" fund calculates only one single NAV per share, which is used for all capital activities regardless whether inflows or outflows are affected. However there are three different main methods for calculating the single NAV. Therefore, if it is a single pricing fund, please also fill out field "OFST401003 Single Pricing Type".
Values - "single pricing" ; "dual pricing"

columns.name: PRIIPS_CATEGORY_VAL

PRIIP Category of the Portfolio as outlined in the Regularly Technical Standards (RTS) of Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 in Annex 2, numbers 4-7.

columns.name: PRIIPS_KID_INVESTMENT_DESC

columns.name: PRIIPS_REFERENCE_INVESTMENT_AMOUNT_VAL

columns.name: PRODUCT_BENCHMARK_CAVEATS

columns.name: PRODUCT_BENCHMARK_NAME_FOR_FACTSHEETS
columns.comment: PMC Definition: An abbreviated version of the benchmark full name which is used for Factsheets and other areas where a character restriction applies

columns.name: PRODUCT_BENCHMARK_TYPE
columns.comment: PMC Field: Defines how the benchmark is used for performance monitoring purposes i.e. whether it is a formal benchmark which performance is measured against, an indicative comparator or a reference index for illustrative purposes.  Used in conjunction with the Investment Objective, primarily in the construction of factsheets.

columns.name: PRODUCT_BENCHMARK_TYPE_INDEX_FUNDS_VAL
columns.comment: Defines how the benchmark is used for performance monitoring purposes i.e. whether it is a formal benchmark which performance is measured against, an indicative comparator or a reference index for illustrative purposes.  Used in conjunction with the Investment Objective, primarily in the construction of factsheets.

columns.name: PRODUCT_LAUNCH_DATE

columns.name: PRODUCT_MEETS_CLIMATE_TRANSITION_BENCHMARK_LIST_EXCLUSIONARY_REQUIREMENTS_VAL

columns.name: PRODUCT_MEETS_PARIS_ALIGNED_BENCHMARK_EXCLUSIONARY_REQUIREMENTS_VAL

columns.name: PRODUCT_NAME

columns.name: PRODUCT_PRICE_BASIS

columns.name: PRODUCT_SHORT_CD

columns.name: PRODUCT_SHORT_NAME

columns.name: PRODUCT_STATUS
columns.comment: PMC Definition: Indicates if the Fund is Open, Closed, Closing or Pending Launch

columns.name: PRODUCT_TYPE
columns.comment:
"Is the fund Complex or Standard? A fund is considered as Standard if all the following conditions are met:
- Fund with an official ISIN
- Fund which do not require specific documentation to be submitted to the transfer agent prior to each subsequent trade
- Fund which do not authorize partial redemption
- Fund with performance fees taken out of the NAV
A fund is considered as Complex if any of the above criteria for Standard Funds is not met"

columns.name: PRODUCT_WITHOUT_RETROCESSION_VAL
columns.comment:
Indicates whether the share class pays any inducement in the context of MiFID II.

yes - The share class does not pay any inducement
no - The share class does pay inducement

// The correspondent MiFID II field introduced by the European Working Group with their MiFID Data Dictionary Template (EMT) is:
EMT: 00110_Fund_Share_Class_Without_Retrocession. This is an Indicative EMT field.//

columns.name: PROFESSIONAL_INVESTOR_VAL
columns.comment:
Might this share class from a producer's perspective being marketed to a professional?
Under MiFID regulation, a professional investor is regarded to have the experience, knowledge and expertise to take investment decisions by its own. Therefore, from a target market point of view, if "OFEM010100 EMT Client Type Retail" was answered with "yes", usually this field should be answered with "yes", too.

yes - both Professional Per Se and Elective Professionals are compatible.
no - neither Professional Per Se nor Elective Professionals are compatible.
professional per se - Professional Per Se is compatible but Elective Professionals are not (this is only used if the distinction "Per Se" is made in the Prospectus)
elective professional - Elective Professional is compatible but Professionals Per Se are not.

columns.name: RECOMMENDED_HOLDING_PERIOD_VAL
columns.comment: The Recommended Holding Period (RHP) represents the view of the PRIIP manufacturer regarding a recommended period of time for a retail investor to hold the product. The RHP is also used as part of the calculation process of some of the metrics displayed within PRIIPs material (e.g. the KID).

columns.name: REGULATOR_CSSF_ID
columns.comment: A unique identifier assigned by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) regulator to the Product. The authority responsible for regulating and overseeing the professionals and products of the Luxembourg financial market.

columns.name: REGULATOR_FCA_ID
columns.comment: A unique identifier assigned by the FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) regulator to the Product. The authority responsible for regulating and overseeing certain aspects of financial markets and institutions.

columns.name: REPLICATION_METHODOLOGY_FIRST_LEVEL
columns.comment: Replication methodology for ETFs or passive funds. This field is linked to OFST191 Replication Methodology Second Level, that specifies the details of this field. Please note, that one can use this field (OFST19) without completing field OFST191 Replication Methodology Second Level, whereas this is not possible for the other way around.

columns.name: REPLICATION_METHODOLOGY_FIRST_LEVEL_VAL
columns.comment:
Replication methodology for ETFs or passive funds. This field is linked to OFST191 Replication Methodology Second Level, that specifies the details of this field. Please note, that one can use this field (OFST19) without completing field OFST191 Replication Methodology Second Level, whereas this is not possible for the other way around.
Values for Replication Methodology First Level would be "physical" ; "synthetical" ; "others"

columns.name: RESPONSIBLE_OWNER_OF_OPERATING_EXPENSES
columns.comment: Which party is responsible for paying operating expenses

columns.name: RETAIL_INVESTOR_VAL
columns.comment: Might this share class from a producer's perspective being marketed to a retail investor no matter, if the investor has only basic knowledge ("OFEM020100 EMT Investor With Basic Knowledge" = yes) or if he is an informed investor ("OFEM020200 EMT Informed Investor" = yes) or is an advanced investor ("OFEM020300 EMT Advanced Investor" = yes)?

columns.name: RETURN_PROFILE_GER_PENSION_SCHEME_VAL
columns.comment: According to rule from the EMT, please use the value "yes" for funds used in German pension contracts, such as Riester and Rürup. For funds with performance fees, please use "neutral" or "no". For other funds, "yes" or "neutral" should be used.

columns.name: RETURN_PROFILE_GROWTH_VAL
columns.comment: May a fund distributor sell this fund to an end investor, whose return profile is 'capital growth'?

columns.name: RETURN_PROFILE_INCOME_VAL
columns.comment: May a fund distributor sell this fund to an end investor, whose return profile is 'income'?

columns.name: RETURN_PROFILE_OPTIONS_OR_LEVERAGE_VAL
columns.comment: May a fund distributor sell this fund to an end investor, whose investment strategy is very aggressive?

columns.name: RETURN_PROFILE_PRESERVATION_VAL
columns.comment: May a fund distributor sell this fund to an end investor, whose return profile is 'capital preservation'?

columns.name: REVIEW_DATE_OF_UNDERLYING_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_DISCLOSED_EXPENSES
columns.comment: The date of the last review of the external manager expenses.

columns.name: RTG_FITCH
columns.comment: Measures the ability of a fund or issuer to repay debt, highlighting credit risk.

columns.name: RTG_MOODY
columns.comment: Assesses the credit risk of a fund or issuer, focusing on the probability of default and expected financial loss.

columns.name: RTG_SP
columns.comment: S&P (Standard & Poor’s) Fund Rating. Evaluates the creditworthiness of a fund or issuer, indicating the likelihood they will meet their financial obligations.

columns.name: SALESFORCE_PRODUCT_ID
columns.comment: This field is named “Product Master: ID” in Salesforce – this is auto generated unique ID, and is assigned to each product in Salesforce (e.g., SEGs, CITs, LLC, and Mutual Funds).  An example of this ID, a0F4U00000LgJAD.

columns.name: SCOPE_DEALING_RESTRICTIONS
columns.comment: PMC Field - this field details any internal notes that have been applied to SCOPE in respect of any dealing restrictions that may be applied to investors

columns.name: SCOPE_HOLDING_RESTRICTIONS
columns.comment: PMC Field - this field details any internal notes that have been applied to SCOPE in respect of any restrictions that may be applied to certain types of investors

columns.name: SCOPE_PRODUCT_CD
columns.comment: A SCOPE system fund identifier consisting of one, two or four letters

columns.name: SDR_SUSTAINABILITY_LABEL
columns.comment: Defines which of the SDR Sustainability Labels the fund is authorised to use. UK’s Sustainability Disclosure Requirements (SDR) defines four labels that funds can use, with specific requirements for each label.

columns.name: SEDOL
columns.comment: A dummy SEDOL code which is displayed on factsheets for Workplace funds

columns.name: SEED_DATE
columns.comment: Date in which client/fund first invests

columns.name: SETTLEMENT_PERIOD_FOR_REDEMPTIONS
columns.comment: How many days are needed to settle a redemption of this fund after the closing/valuation date, i.e. how many days does it take after valuation until the cash is transferred to the sellers account ? Please choose calendar or business days in field "OFST430200 Calendar Or Business Days For Transactions".

columns.name: SETTLEMENT_PERIOD_FOR_SUBSCRIPTIONS
columns.comment: The number of days after the trade date on which subscriptions settle.                                                                                                                PMC Defintion - The number of days after the trade date on which PMC pays the underlying manager

columns.name: SFDR_CLASSIFICATION
columns.comment: The classification of the Fund in relation to the SFDR Directive. Classifications are categorised based on How ESG is   integrated into the Fund.

columns.name: SHAREHOLDER_VAL
columns.comment: Indicates whether investors invest in the sub-fund directly, via a PMC or both

columns.name: SPREAD_ANTI_DILUTION_LEVY_BID
columns.comment: Protects existing investors from the costs incurred due to large inflows or outflows of money into or out of the fund.

columns.name: SPREAD_ANTI_DILUTION_LEVY_DATE
columns.comment: Effective date of Spread / Anti Dilution Levy

columns.name: SPREAD_ANTI_DILUTION_LEVY_OFFER
columns.comment: Protects existing investors from the costs incurred due to large inflows or outflows of money into or out of the fund.

columns.name: SPREAD_ANTI_DILUTION_LEVY_ROUND_TRIP
columns.comment: Protects existing investors from the costs incurred due to large inflows or outflows of money into or out of the fund.

columns.name: SRI
columns.comment: PMC field: Summary Risk Indicator (SRI) is a standardized risk indicator under PRIIPS regulation that considers both the volatility of a financial instrument (market risk) and the creditworthiness of the issuer (credit risk). It is displayed as a number between 1 and 7, representing the combined risk of the product.

columns.name: SRRI
columns.comment: The Synthetic Risk and Reward Indicator (SRRI) demonstrates the relative risk and reward profile of the fund.  Used for Workplace Funds only and displayed on their factsheet.

columns.name: SUB_GROUPING_VAL
columns.comment: Further granularity of the asset types within the Fund's investment profile

columns.name: SUBSCRIPTION_CRRNCY
columns.comment: The currency that investors use to subscribe to the Fund. The majority of Funds are either £ or €

columns.name: SUBSCRIPTION_FREQUENCY
columns.comment: The timeframes in which investors can subscribe. E.g. there is an annual window whereby investors can subscribe. For closed ended Funds this will likely be a finite period.

columns.name: SUBSCRIPTION_METHOD
columns.comment: Method by which investors subscribe / invest capital into the Fund

columns.name: SYSTEM_BENCHMARK_ID
columns.comment: Fundipedia assigned code specific to the Benchmark. This code is unique at Benchmark level only. (This is a primary key to link Product and Benchmark)

columns.name: SYSTEM_STRATEGY_ID
columns.comment: Fundipedia assigned code specific to the Product. This code is unique at Product level only. (This is a primary key to link tables to Product)

columns.name: SYSTEM_UMBRELLA_ID
columns.comment: Fundipedia assigned code specific to the umbrella. This code is unique at umbrella level only. (This is a primary key to link Product and Umbrella)

columns.name: TARGET_MARKET_DESC
columns.comment: Describes the suitability of the Fund for schemes and clients. This is presented as 'Who Is This Fund For?' on the Fact Sheet and the "Intended Retail Investor" section of KIDS.

columns.name: TARGET_RETURN_TYPE
columns.comment: The target return type of the Fund. This can either be where the Fund has a formal benchmark or uses a performance metric, such as IRR.

columns.name: TIER_1_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 1 Bps is used in determining the management fee. If not populated, Tier 1 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels.

columns.name: TIER_2_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 2 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than Tier 1 MV. If not populated, Tier 2 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above Tier 1 MV.

columns.name: TIER_3_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 3 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than the sum of previous Tiers. If not populated, Tier 3 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above the sum of previous tiers.

columns.name: TIER_4_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 4 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than the sum of previous Tiers. If not populated, Tier 4 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above the sum of previous tiers.

columns.name: TIER_5_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 5 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than the sum of previous Tiers. If not populated, Tier 5 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above the sum of previous tiers.

columns.name: TIER_6_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 6 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than the sum of previous Tiers. If not populated, Tier 6 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above the sum of previous tiers.

columns.name: TIER_7_MV
columns.comment: The market value (in [$]M) break point for which Tier 7 Bps is used in determining the management fee, applicable to accounts larger than the sum of previous Tiers. If not populated, Tier 7 Bps is a flat fee assessed across all asset levels above the sum of previous tiers.

columns.name: TOTAL_EXPENSE_RATIO
columns.comment: A measure of the total costs  associated with managing and operating an investment fund against the value of the fund's total assets.

columns.name: TPA_FAND_CD
columns.comment: CITI generated identifier at Product level.

columns.name: TYPE_OF_EU_DIRECTIVE
columns.comment: Indicates, whether the fund is an UCITS as outlined in EU Directives 2009/65/EC or an AIF as described in the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive 2011/61/EU

columns.name: UCITS_ELIGIBILITY_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether the shares or units in the CIS (fund) are eligible to be held by a UCITS.

columns.name: UCITS_GLOBAL_EXPOSURE_LIMIT
columns.comment: Indicates the global exposure limit the product must adhere to.

columns.name: UCITS_GLOBAL_EXPOSURE_TYPE_VAL
columns.comment:
Calculation methodology used to measure global exposure. Global exposure, as referred to in Article 51(3) of the UCITS Directive, is a measure designed to limit either the incremental exposure and leverage generated by a UCITS through the use of financial derivative instruments (including embedded derivatives) or the market risk of the UCITS portfolio. 
Incremental exposure and leverage are more precisely linked to UCITS utilising the commitment approach and that global exposure for UCITS using a VaR approach is linked to market risk.

columns.name: UCITS_KIID_INVESTMENT_DESC
columns.comment: Narrative text outlining the rules and policies that govern the Product and how investments can be made by its share or unit classes. This version of the investment policy is included in the UCITS KIID.

columns.name: UCITS_KIID_SFDR_CLASSIFICATION
columns.comment: The SFDR sub-classification the Fund falls into. This is used as a marker to indicate the relevant narrative to be included in the UCITS KIID

columns.name: UK_FACTSHEET_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if a UK Fact Sheet is produced for the Fund. Please note that PMC are not required to produce factsheets. Fund Reporting Team need to agree to support factsheet production.

columns.name: UK_FUND_CENTRE_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the fund appears on the UK Fund Centre website.

columns.name: UK_NET_CHARGES_FACTSHEET_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if a net of charges factsheet (typically produced for UK DC schemes) is produced for the Fund

columns.name: UK_PRIIP_OR_UCITS_OR_BOTH_DATA_DELIVERY_VAL
columns.comment:
Indicates if the record contains UK PRIIPs data, UCITS data or Both. This field is only required if providing some UK data in the delivery, otherwise it can be left blank.

//The correspondent PRIIP field introduced by FinDatEx with their European PRIIPS Template v2.1 (EPT) is: EPT: 08010_UK_PRIIP_Or_UCITS_Or_Both_data_delivery//

columns.name: UK_REPORTING_CRRNCY
columns.comment: The currency which is used for reporting purposes on UK factsheets and on the fund centre. NB not the same as base currency which is always GBP for PMC.

columns.name: UK_UCITS_FUND_IND
columns.comment: Is the fund a UK-authorised UCITS? Such funds are UK-domiciled funds that would have had the value 'UCITS' in field OFST160040 Type of EU Directive prior to the Implementation Period Completion Day (IPCD) of the withdrawal of the United Kingdom (UK) from the European Union (EU), and should have the value 'AIF' in that field post-IPCD. The IPCD is defined in the EU (Withdrawal Agreement) Act 2020 as 31 December 2020 at 11pm (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2020/1/contents/enacted).

columns.name: UNDERLYING_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_DISCLOSED_ADDITIONAL_EXPENSES_NOT_INCLUDE_PER
columns.comment: The Additional Expense rate as disclosed by the External Manager at a given date confirmed in last expenses reviewed field. Please refer to the field 'Underlying External Product Disclosed Expenses Additional Info'. Other fees may apply.

columns.name: UNDERLYING_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_DISCLOSED_EXPENSES_ADDITIONAL_INFO
columns.comment: Additional expense information disclosed by the External Manager that is not captured under AMC, Additional Expenses or Property Expenses.

columns.name: UNDERLYING_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_DISCLOSED_PROPERTY_EXPENSES_APPLICABLE
columns.comment: The Property Expenses as disclosed by the External Manager at a given date confirmed in last expenses reviewed field. Please refer to the field 'Underlying External Product Disclosed Expenses Additional Info'. Other fees may apply.

columns.name: UNDERLYING_PRODUCT_STRUCTURE
columns.comment: PMC Defintion - The legal structure of the underlying fund.

columns.name: UPPER_RANGE_OF_RETURN_TARGET
columns.comment: Higher range of return e.g. if 7%-9% then 9%

columns.name: VALUATION_FREQ
columns.comment: Interval between the valuation of the fund

columns.name: VALUATION_POINT
columns.comment: The valuation time at which the NAV of the fund is calculated. Please also indicate the Time Zone in the field "OFST1251 Fund Valuation Point Time Zone".

columns.name: VALUE_FOR_MONEY_FURTHER_INFORMATION
columns.comment:
Link to sources of relevant information. This may provide a link to information to explain a "2" in fields OFEM090500 or OFEM090600 and may be used to explain OFEM090700 further.

For example, a hyperlink to the COLL assessment of value report, other relevant information, relevant NCA website, or an email address.

// The correspondent MiFID II field introduced by the European Working Group with their MiFID Data Dictionary Template (EMT) is:
EMT: 09080_Further_Information_UK. This is an Optional EMT field.//

columns.name: VALUE_FOR_MONEY_NEXT_REVIEW_DUE_DATE
VALUE_FOR_MONEY_REVIEW_DATE
columns.comment:
Date of value assessment review or date COLL assessment of value report published or initial launch date. OFEM090300 EMT Data Reporting VFM UK is set to "yes".

Use initial launch date where the initial assessment has not yet become subject to review or where the first COLL assessment of value report has yet to be published. Should not be later than date in OFEM000050 EMT Date And Time Of File Generation. Note PRIN 2A.4.5R.

// The correspondent MiFID II field introduced by the European Working Group with their MiFID Data Dictionary Template (EMT) is:
EMT: 09090_Review_Date_UK. This is a Conditional EMT field.//

columns.name: WRAPPER_QUASAR_CD
columns.comment: The Quasar code of the wrapper PMC Fund.

columns.name: WRAPPER_SCOPE_CD
columns.comment: The SCOPE code of the wrapper PMC Fund.

columns.name: BENCHMARK_ID
columns.comment: The LGIM identifier of the Benchmark associated with the relationship.

columns.name: SYSTEM_PRODUCT_ID
columns.comment: The Fundipedia internal ID of the Product associated with the relationship.

columns.name: BENCHMARK_ROLE
columns.comment:
Indicates the Role of the Benchmark in relation to the associated Product. Definitions of "ESG Reporting" and "Primary" as follows:

ESG Alternative benchmark used for ESG reporting purposes to demonstrate the ESG credentials of a fund. Where it is different to the primary benchmark, it is often the ‘parent’ benchmark of the primary benchmark.

This is the primary benchmark as stated in a fund's prospectus. If a primary benchmark is not given, this field will be blank.

columns.comment: Service Code

columns.comment: Fundipedia assigned code specific to the Product. This code is unique at Product level only. (This is a primary key to link tables to Product)

columns.comment: Service Code defining the data provider

columns.comment: Business Date of Data Snapshot

columns.name: CTB_OR_PAB_APPLIES
columns.comment: Indicates whether the Products aligns to PAB (EU Paris-aligned Benchmark)' or CTB (EU Climate Transition Benchmark).

columns.name: ECOLABEL_APPLIES
columns.comment: Identifies if the EU label for retail products applies, the label identifies if the product has met a minimum ecological criteria as defined by the EU.

columns.name: ESG_TILTED_INDEX_APPLIES
columns.comment: Identifies if the product utilises an Index that has been tilted based on ESG factors.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_CONVENTIONAL_WEAPONS_SUPPLEMENTARY_DETAILS
columns.comment: Conventional weapons are weapons categories that are not controversial weapons or nuclear wepeans. This field details any conventional weapons categories that are to be excluded from its investments.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_ESG_EXCLUSIONS_APPLY
columns.comment: Identifies if the product implements any ESG exclusions to exclude companies that meet a given set of criteria from its investments.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_LGIM_CLIMATE_IMPACT_PLEDGE_APPLIES
columns.comment: Confirms if the product applies exclusions from the LGIM Climate Impact Pledge. The LGIM Climate Impact Pledge aims to help companies support efforts to limit carbon emissions to net zero by 2050.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_LGIM_COAL_POLICY_APPLIES
columns.comment: The LGIM Coal policy sets out the critieria for identifying companies with involvement in Coal and their subsidiaries to be excluded from its investments. This field identifies if the coal policy is applicable to the product.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_LGIM_CONTROVERSIAL_WEAPONS_POLICY_APPLIES
columns.comment: This field identifies if the Controversial Weapons policy is applicable to the product. The LGIM Controversial Weapons policy sets out the critieria for identifying companies involved in Controversial weapons to be excluded from its investments.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_LGIM_FWPL_EXCLUSIONS_APPLIES
columns.comment: This field indicates if exclusions are applied to the product to exclude companies from being purchased or held based on LGIM Future World Protection List (FWPL) is a list of companies that fail to meet minimum standards of globally accepted business practices,as determined by LGIM.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_LGIM_SDG_EXCLUSIONS_APPLY
columns.comment: This field indicates if investment exclusions are applied to the product based on LGIM SDG (Sustainable Development Goals) score.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_SOLACTIVE_ESG_ENHANCED_INDEX_EXCLUSIONS_APPLIES
columns.comment: Details whether the Product excludes Companies from its investments based on the Solactive ESG Enhanced methodology.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_SOLACTIVE_ESG_INDEX_EXCLUSIONS_APPLIES
columns.comment: Details whether the Product excludes Companies from its investments based on the Solactive ESG methodology.

columns.name: EXCLUSIONS_SUPPLEMENTARY_DETAILS
columns.comment: Free text field where additional exclusions information can be captured outside the other true/false and list of values fields related exclusion fields.

columns.name: IMPACT_ESG_STRATEGY_APPLIES
columns.comment: Identifies whether the Product applies an ESG Impact strategy (i.e. Womens Empowerment, Poverty, Carbon capture).

columns.name: LGIM_NET_ZERO_FRAMEWORK_ALIGNMENT_VAL
columns.comment: Identifies if the Product aligns to the LGIM Net Zero Framework which aims to reach net zero greenhouse gases by 2050 and other factors considered including carbon intensity and temperature alignment.

columns.name: BVI_SUSTAINABILITY_CLASSIFICATION_CD
columns.comment: BVI represents the interests of the German fund industry at national and international level. This field reflects the ESG label of the product provided by the BVI.

columns.name: MIN_EU_TAXONOMY_ALIGNMENT_PERCENTAGE
columns.comment: The minimum committment of investments that are considered environmentally sustainable and algined with the SFDR taxonomy in the context of the Sustainable Asset Allocation.

columns.name: PRODUCT_SPECIFIC_ENGAGEMENT_APPLIES
columns.comment: This field indicates whether there is specific engagement defined as part of this product. Where LGIM engages with the companies in which LGIM invests, to address risks and opportunities – both company-specific and market-wide.

columns.name: SFDR_ARTICLE_CLASSIFICATION
SFDR_MIN_SUSTAINABLE_INVESTMENT_PERCENTAGE
columns.comment: The minimum commitment of investments that are considered sustainable in the context of the Sustainable Asset Allocation for SFDR.

columns.name: SFDR_OPTIONAL_PAI_INDICATOR_VAL
columns.comment: This field captures any optional PAI indicators that are applicable to the product as per SFDR.

columns.name: TARGET_IMPACT_SUPPLEMENTARY_DETAILS
columns.comment: Details the ESG target impact strategy that the Product adheres to (i.e. Womens Empowerment, Poverty, Carbon capture).

columns.name: THEMATIC_ESG_STRATEGY_APPLIES
columns.comment: Identifies whether the Product applies an ESG Thematic strategy (i.e. Carbon Removals, Green Bonds).

columns.name: AMOUNT

columns.name: BASIS

columns.name: ACCRUAL_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: Accrual type for accrual generating securities (ex. Variable Rate, Interest At Maturity). Relevant to DEBT investment class. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'ACCRUALTYP'; for Credit Linked Notes DESC_TYPE = 'CLNACRUTYP'.

columns.name: ACCRUED_CALCULATION_INTEREST_RATE
columns.comment: Interest rate used to calculate the accrued interest in the current period.

columns.name: ACCRUED_FACTOR_DESC
columns.comment: Provides the Accrued Factor (DY202, ACCRUED_FACTOR) type. If the Accrued Factor is a combination of more than one factor, then the description "Accrued Factor" is returned. If only one factor is involved, then the description reflects the nature of the factor.

columns.name: ADR_PER_SHARE
columns.comment: Ratio of how many ADRs represent 1 share of the underlying security.

columns.name: AMT_ISSUED
columns.comment: The quantity/amount issued.

columns.name: AMT_OUTST
columns.comment: Quantity/Amount/Shares outstanding. If populated SHARES_OUTST_EFF_DATE defines the effective date of value populated in AMT_OUTST.

columns.name: ANNOUNCEMENT_DATE
columns.comment: Latest Full Earnings Report Date

columns.name: ANNUAL_DIV
columns.comment: The annual dividend.

columns.name: ANY_INDEX_FLAG
columns.comment: Security UDF Text 45. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR45

columns.name: ASSET_CRRNCY_CD
columns.comment: Asset currency code.

columns.name: AVG_DAILY_VOL
columns.comment: Number of contracts traded on a particular stock exchange during the reporting period divided by the number of trading days for the period as reported by the company. Unit: Millions.

columns.name: BAIL_IN_BOND_DESIGNATION
columns.comment: Indicates whether the security is defined as a bail-in or resolution note by the issuer and/or in the credit agreement and/or relevant national authority rules, such as the US Federal Reserve System (US FED) final rules and/or credit ratings.

columns.name: BB_GLOBAL_ID
columns.comment: Bloomberg Global ID, a unique identifier assigned to instruments of all asset classes.

columns.name: BB_UNIQUE_ID
columns.comment: Bloomberg Unique ID that identifies an instrument within a trading venue.

columns.name: BB_YELLOW_KEY
columns.comment: The name of the market sector yellow key on the Bloomberg Terminal the security is located under. Non-US government bonds will return 'Corp' instead of 'Govt' as this security type is stored under the 'Corp' sector yellow key as a default.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_1_SECTOR_NAME
columns.comment: BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System) LEVEL 1 Sector. Returns the Bloomberg Industry Classification System (BICS) level 1 name.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_2_INDUSTRY_GROUP_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System) LEVEL 2 Industry Group.
Returns the Bloomberg Industry Classification System (BICS) level 2 name.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_3_INDUSTRY_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System) LEVEL 3 Industry.
Returns the Bloomberg Industry Classification System (BICS) level 3 name.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_4_SUB_INDUSTRY_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System) LEVEL 4 Sub Industry.
Returns the Bloomberg Industry Classification System (BICS) level 4 name.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_5_SEGMENT_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System). 
Returns the Bloomberg Industry Classification System (BICS) level 5 name.

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_6_SEGMENT_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System).

columns.name: BICS_LEVEL_7_SEGMENT_NAME
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System).

columns.name: BOND_RECOVERY_RATE
columns.comment: Assumed recovery percentage of principal when the bond is defaulted.

columns.name: BUS_DAY_CONV
columns.comment: Code corresponding to a business day convention used by the security (in relation to any particular date defined by security terms and conditions). Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'DAYADJCONV'.

columns.name: CALC_EURO_TYPE_DESC
columns.comment: Description representing the issuer and/or type of the debt security. Description defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'CALCEROTP2'.

columns.name: CALC_PERIOD_FREQ_CD
columns.comment: Calculation Period Frequency

columns.name: CALC_TYPE
columns.comment: The calculation type is the method used to determine the cash flows, accrued interest, and price/yield of a fixed income security based on various market conventions and security structures.

columns.name: CALC_TYPE_DESC
columns.comment: Method used to determine the cash flows, accrued interest, and price/yield of a fixed income security based on various market conventions and security structures.

columns.name: CALCULATED_MATURITY_DATE
columns.comment: Indicates the maturity being used in calculations. This field will match Maturity (DS035, MATURITY for all securities except perpetual issues. Perpetuals will use a rolling maturity of approximately 149 years from the settlement date.

columns.name: CALL_ANNOUNCEMENT_DATE
columns.comment: The date on which the issuer announced that the bond will be called. The bond will be redeemed within a period of time that is greater than or equal to the call notice days.

columns.name: CALL_BUSINESS_DAYS_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the call days notice is expressed in business days. Returns true if the call notice is expressed in business days, otherwise, the field returns false.

columns.name: CALL_DATE
columns.comment: The next call date.

columns.name: CALL_DISCRETE_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the instrument is discretely callable. A discretely callable instrument can only be exercised on specific dates. Call Schedule - Discrete will change from 'N' to 'Y' when Completely Called Indicator (DS559, COMPLETELY_CALLED) =Y.

columns.name: CALL_FEATURE
columns.comment: Provides the number of times in any given year the call option can be exercised. In the case of a bond where the call can only be exercised once in its lifetime, onetime is returned.  In the case of a bond where the call option can be exercised on any unspecified date, anytime is returned. For securities callable on an irregular basis or with multi-year frequencies (i.e. 5 year frequency) the field will return a null value.

columns.name: CALL_FREQ
columns.comment: The number of times per year a call can be exercised.        A return of '0' is applicable on securities that are either:    1. continuously callable, (DX037, Call Feature = Anytime) or     2. is callable once, (DX037, Call Feature = Onetime) or    3. has a multi-year frequency (i.e. 5 year frequency)    4. is callable on an irregular basis (bi-weekly, dates without a pattern)

columns.name: CALL_NOTICE_DAYS
columns.comment: The number of calendar days advance notice that an issuer must give to the investor before calling a bond. This is typically associated with American-style calls and make whole calls. A typical advance notice is 30 days, but 10, 15, 45 days are also seen in the field.

columns.name: CALL_TYPE
columns.comment: A return of 'Callable' indicates the issue has an optional call provision. The Extraordinary Redemption Flag (DS594, XO_REDEMP_FLAG) will indicate if the bonds are subject to extraordinary redemption provisions and the Make Whole Call Indicator (DS754, MAKE_WHOLE_CALL) will indicate if the bonds have a make whole call provision. If your only Redemption Provisions are the Extraordinary Redemption and/or a make Whole Call your Call Type (DS558, CALL_TYP)= NON-CALLABLE.

columns.name: CALLABLE_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether the security has a call provision.        Corps:       Indicates whether the security is subject to early redemption through a call provision, excluding extraordinary redemptions, sinking fund redemptions, or make-whole call redemptions. To check whether the bond is still callable, is beyond all of its discrete call dates or has been called already, check the Security Still Callable Indicator (DX815, IS_STILL_CALLABLE).         Loans:       Indicates whether or not the loan has call protection. Generally, all loans are continuously callable (can be called at any time) without penalty. If there is call protection on the loan, the borrower would pay the lenders a premium if they were to repay or refinance (in whole or in part) the loan prior to maturity. Call protection typically steps down to par according to a Call Schedule (SC001, CALL_SCHEDULE).        Mortgages:       Indicates if the collateral is subject to a cleanup call Mtge Deal (DS795, MTG_DEAL_CALL_PCT) and/or the bond is subject to a specified call date Next Call Date (DS022, NXT_CALL_DT).        Municipals:      Indicates whether the security is subject to early redemption through a call provision, excluding extraordinary redemptions, sinking fund redemptions, or make-whole call redemptions.

columns.name: CALLED_DATE
columns.comment: Date which the issuer has fully redeemed the bond prior to maturity via the company's call option.        Municipals:    Date which the issuer has fully redeemed the bond prior to maturity via the issuer or borrower's fully executed call or tender option.

columns.name: CALLED_PRICE
columns.comment: The price which the issuer paid to redeem the bond prior to maturity via the company's call option.        Municipals:    Price which the issuer or borrower paid to fully execute the call or tender option bond prior to maturity.

columns.name: CASH_EQ_IND
columns.comment: Cash_Eq Indicator

columns.name: CASH_IND
columns.comment: Cash Indicator

columns.name: CASH_SETTLED
columns.comment: Indicates if the contract can have a cash settlement. The cash value of the underlying asset is delivered to satisfy the contract.

columns.name: CDS_DEBT_TYPE_CD
columns.comment: CDS Debt Type

columns.name: CFI_CD
columns.comment: Classification of Financial Instruments code (ISO 10962).

columns.name: CIC_CD
columns.comment: Complementary Identification Code

columns.name: CLIP
columns.comment: CUSIP-linked MIP code (CLIP) is used in the financial derivatives markets to identify the reference entity of a credit default swap.[1] It is mainly used as a key field in Markit's reference entity database (RED). Each CLIP is linked with one or more CUSIPs each representing reference entity obligations (securities).

columns.name: CNTRCT_SIZE
columns.comment: Security contract size i.e. number of trading units for derivative instruments (ex. options, futures).

columns.name: CNTRY_OF_RISK_CD
columns.comment: Country code of risk

columns.name: CNTRY_OF_RISK_ISO_2

Two character ISO country of risk code.

columns.name: CNTRY_OF_RISK_ISO_3

Three character ISO country of risk code.

columns.comment: Country name of Risk

columns.name: COLLATERAL_CNTRY_CD
columns.comment: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) code for the country of the collateral group backing the security. If there is more than one country, 'Mixed' will be displayed. This field is reported as of issuance.

columns.name: COLLATERAL_CNTRY_ISO_2
columns.comment:
Two character ISO collateral country code.

columns.name: COLLATERAL_CNTRY_ISO_3
columns.comment:
Three character ISO collateral country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: COLLATERAL_CNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Country name of Collateral

columns.name: COLLATERAL_TYPE
columns.comment: Nature of what underlies or backs the liability the security represents.

columns.name: COMMENTS
columns.comment: Free-form comments.

columns.name: COMPOSITE_FIGI
columns.comment: Twelve character, alphanumeric identifier. The first 2 characters are upper-case consonants (including 'Y'), the third character is the upper-case 'G', characters 4 -11 are any upper-case consonant (including 'Y') or integer between 0 and 9, and the last character is a check-digit. The Composite level of assignment is provided in cases where there are multiple trading venues for the instrument within a single country or market. The Composite Financial Instrument Global Identifier (FIGI) enables users to link multiple FIGIs at the trading venue-level within the same country or market in order to obtain an aggregated view for that instrument within that country or market.  Note: Where an MTF trades multiple listings, this field will indicate the MTF as composite and the true associated market level is indicated in MTF Assc Mkt Comp Financial Instrument Global ID (ID241, MTF_ASSC_MKT_COMP_ID_BB_GLOBAL).

columns.name: CONTINGENT_CONVERSION_IND
columns.comment: For a convertible security, indicates the conversion is conditioned on the price of the underlying being greater than the specified trigger.  A Contingent Conversion is also commonly known as (COCO).

columns.name: CONTRACT_MONTH
columns.comment: Contract month of the future product in MM format.

columns.name: CONTRACT_YEAR
columns.comment: Contract Year of the future product in YYYY format.

columns.name: CONVERTIBLE
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether the security is convertible.

columns.name: COUPON_AS_OF_DATE
columns.comment: As of date of the most recently reported coupon for floating rate notes or securities with a variable coupon rate  having a coupon date prior to the settlement date. Otherwise, the initial interest accrual date (DS137, INT_ACC_DT) is returned.        For Mortgages, the as of date returned will be nominal (not adjusted for business days).        For fixed rate United States (US) Governments (Govts), will display the Issue Date (DS031, ISSUE_DT).

columns.name: COUPON_RATE
columns.comment: The coupon rate (required for coupon debt instruments) or discount (required for discount notes).

columns.name: COVERED_IND
columns.comment: Debt securities that are issued by specialized credit institutions with a narrowly defined scope of business activities, such as mortgage and public sector lending, and backed by a cover pool, or pool of assets (often mortgages or public sector loans) which are used as collateral for covered bond debt instruments and to which investors have a preferential claim in the event of default.

columns.name: CPI_REFERENCE
columns.comment: Reference to the inflation index.

columns.name: CPN_PAY_CNVTN
columns.comment: The Floating Rate Note (FRN) coupon pay convention code specifies coupon and payment schedules not supported by the coupon date parameters. It indicates how to compute the coupon date, and also describes a lag between the coupon date and the actual payment of the coupon. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'RESET_CNVN'.

columns.name: CPN_PAY_CNVTN_DESC
columns.comment: The Floating Rate Note (FRN) coupon pay convention description specifies coupon and payment schedules not supported by the coupon date parameters. It indicates how to compute the coupon date, and also describes a lag between the coupon date and the actual payment of the coupon.

columns.name: CPN_TYPE
columns.comment: Specifies how the periodic payment is structured. Under specific scenarios, payment structure details are replaced with information detailing the state of the instrument (Defaulted, Exchanged, Flat Trading, Funged, Prelim, When Issued).

columns.name: CREDIT_ENHANCEMENT
columns.comment: Name of the insurance or other program that backs the debt service on the bonds and enhances their credit quality.        Mortgages:       Classifies which credit enhancement approach was applied to non-agency deals.  Possible return values are 'OC' (over-collateralized) and '6 pack'.  OC is the excess of collateral over bonds, and 6 pack is a shifting interest structure in which principal prepayments are allocated disproportionately to the trust's senior certificates.

columns.name: CREDIT_LINKED_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the security is Credit Linked

columns.name: CROS_CRRNCY_MTM_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether a cross currency instrument exchanges notional adjustments on each reset date based on FX movements.

columns.name: CRRNCY_PAIR
columns.comment: A currency pair is the quotation of two different currencies, with the value of one currency being quoted against the other. The first listed currency of a currency pair is called the base currency, and the second currency is called the quote currency.

columns.name: CRRNCY_PAIR_RATE
columns.comment: The currency pair rate

columns.name: CURRENT_COMMITMENT
columns.comment: Current commitment amount.

columns.name: CURRENT_COUPON_RATE
columns.comment: Current period's interest rate for the security.  Available for floating rate securities. This field will typically return the latest value from Floater Coupon History (FL050, FLT_CPN_HIST). For bonds which reset more frequently than they pay, this will return the annualized rate used for accrued interest calculations applicable to the current settlement date.

columns.name: CURRENT_SHARES_OUTSTANDING_UNROUNDED
columns.comment: Total current number of shares outstanding. This data may have been obtained from annual, semi-annual, and quarterly reports, Edgar filings, press releases, or stock exchanges. The value is the unrounded real value. See Shares Outstanding (BS081, BS_SH_OUT) for historical shares outstanding as of period end date and Current Shares Outstanding (DS124 EQY_SH_OUT) for daily shares out. In most countries, the number of shares outstanding may include treasury shares, if any. Where disclosure allows, Bloomberg makes best efforts to remove both cancelled and treasury shares on a timely basis. Shares out from all stock exchanges of the following countries exclude treasury shares from the number of shares outstanding. Please reference DS555, EQY_PRIM_SECURITY_COMP_EXCH for the composite exchange code of the primary security: Argentina (AR) , Bahamas (BM), Bangladesh (BD), Barbados (BA), Bermuda (BH), Canada (CN), China (CH) Georgia (GG), Guernsey-Channel Islands (GU), India (IN), Israel (IT), Ireland (ID), Jamaica (JA), Malaysia (MK), Malta (MV), New Zealand (NZ), Pakistan (PA), Panama (PP), Philippines (PM), Singapore (SP), Sri Lanka (SL), Trinidad and Tobago (TP), United Kingdom (LN), United States (US), Vietnam (VN), Thailand(TB) Shares out is updated on a primary ticker (ID043,ID_BB_PRIM_SECURITY_FLAG as "Y"). Secondary tickers' shares out is not maintained but returns from its primary ticker's shares out. American Depository Receipts (ADR)/Global Depository Receipts (GDR): Number of underlying equivalent shares. For true ADR/GDR shares outstanding, please refer to Current ADRs Outstanding (AD031, ADR_SH_OUT). For units, it is the sum of shares outstanding for all underlying securities divided by the number of securities one unit is made of. The related fields referenced herein may not be available in all enterprise products.

columns.name: CUSIP
columns.comment: The CUSIP of the security.

columns.name: CUSTOM_US_CREDIT_FLAG
columns.comment: Security UDF Text 42. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR42

columns.name: DAY_BASIS
columns.comment: The day basis or day count code. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'DAY_BASIS'.

columns.name: DAY_BASIS_DESC
columns.comment: The description text.

columns.name: DAYS_TO_SETTLE
columns.comment: The number of business days from today to settlement.

columns.name: DEBT_TO_EQUITY_FUNDAMENTAL_TICKER
columns.comment: Returns the equity ticker of the company which has the fundamental data relevant for the loaded debt security.  Returns the issuer's equity ticker if the issuer has fundamental data, otherwise returns the equity ticker of the nearest parent where there is fundamental data.

columns.name: DEFAULT_EXTENSION_MATURITY_DATE
columns.comment: Indicates the extended maturity date for bonds that have been extended at a set price due to a partial or full default.         For covered bonds with a soft-bullet structure, field will return the extendable maturity.         For covered bonds with a pass-through structure, revert to Final Maturity (DX097, FINAL_MATURITY to view the extendable maturity.         Covered bonds with a soft-bullet structure will have the following attributes:     Covered Indicator (DX533, IS_COVERED = Y     Extendible Maturity Date Indicator (DS828, EXTENDIBLE = N     Default Extension Maturity Date (DZ423, DEFAULT_EXTENSION_MATURITY_DATE = Date        Covered bonds with a pass-through structure will have the following attributes:     Covered Indicator (DX533, IS_COVERED = Y     Extendible Maturity Date Indicator (DS828, EXTENDIBLE = Y    Final Maturity (DX097, FINAL_MATURITY = Date

columns.name: DEFAULTED_IND
columns.comment: Defaulted Indicator

columns.name: DEFLATION_FLOOR_IND
columns.comment: Indicates whether the bond has a deflation floor, limiting the downside on inflation.

columns.name: DIV_CRRNCY_CD
columns.comment: The dividend currency code. Code defined in DIM_CURRENCY as CRRNCY_CD.

columns.name: DIVIDEND_PERCENT_FRANKED
columns.comment: Dividend paid by a company out of profits on which the company has already paid tax. The shareholder is entitled to an imputation credit, or reduction in the amount of income tax that must be paid, up to the amount of tax already paid by the company. The % figure represents the % of tax already paid by the company. Sometimes the percentage franked is also referred to in company announcements as a franked amount or imputed credit.

columns.name: DOC_CLAUSE
columns.comment: The code for the terms under which underlying issue is considered in default.

columns.name: DOMICILE_CNTRY_CD
columns.comment: Country of domicile.

columns.name: DOMICILE_CNTRY_ISO_2
columns.comment:
Two character DOMICILE ISO country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: DOMICILE_CNTRY_ISO_3
columns.comment:
Three character DOMICILE ISO country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: DOMICILE_CNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Country name of Domicile

columns.name: DSB_DEBT_SENIORITY
columns.comment: DSB Debt Seniority

columns.name: EQUITY_FISCAL_YEAR_END
columns.comment: Returns the month/year of the last annual financial results announcement date. Companies can choose to report their annual financial results for a 12-month or 52/53 week period not ending on 12/31. For a period ending between the 1st and 15th days of the month, this field will return the prior calendar month.

columns.name: EXDIV_DATE
columns.comment: Ex dividend date.

columns.name: EXDIV_IND
columns.comment: Indicator (Y/N) whether dividends are generated by the debt security.

columns.name: EXPIRE_DATE
columns.comment: The expiration date. Required for swaptions.

columns.name: EXPIRE_SETTLE_DATE
columns.comment: Expiration settlement date for OTC FX Options. Date of final settlement payment for Total Return swaps

columns.name: EXTENDIBLE_MATURITY_DATE_IND
columns.comment: Indicates if the security's maturity date can be extended past its original maturity date by the issuer or bondholder, or insurer (in the case of catastrophe bonds). Excludes soft bullets and conditional extensions. Further, having a Final Maturity (DX097, FINAL_MATURITY) greater than Maturity (DS035, MATURITY) (alone) does not meet the criteria of extendible. Covered bonds with a soft-bullet structure will have the following attributes: *Covered Soft Bullet(DT883, COVERED_SOFT_BULLET) = Y *Extendible Maturity Date Indicator (DS828, EXTENDIBLE) = N *Default Extension Maturity Date (DZ423, DEFAULT_EXTENSION_MATURITY_DATE) = Date Covered bonds with a soft-bullet structure will have the following attributes: *Covered Soft Bullet (DT883, COVERED_SOFT_BULLET) = Y *Extendible Maturity Date Indicator (DS828, EXTENDIBLE) = N *Default Extension Maturity Date (DZ423, DEFAULT_EXTENSION_MATURITY_DATE) = Date Covered bonds with a Pass-Through structure will have the following attributes: * Covered Conditional Pass-Through (DT884, COVERED_CONDITIONAL_PASS_THROUGH) = Y * Extendible Maturity Date Indicator (DS828, EXTENDIBLE) = N * Default Extension Maturity Date (DZ423, DEFAULT_EXTENSION_MATURITY_DATE) = Date

columns.name: FACE_AMT
columns.comment: Face amount shown in thousands (M).

columns.name: FACTOR
columns.comment: Value of the factor

columns.name: FINAL_MATURITY_DATE
columns.comment: The legal final maturity of the bond as stated in the official documentation.

columns.name: FIRST_CALL_ISSUANCE_DATE
columns.comment: First call date of a callable bond, indicated by Call Indicator (DS168, CALLABLE), based on the issuance date.

columns.name: FIRST_COUPON_PERIOD_TYPE
columns.comment: Describes the first coupon period of the bond with respect to the payment frequency (DS034, CPN_FREQ).

columns.name: FIRST_PAYMENT_DATE
columns.comment: The first coupon payment date (required for irregular payment securities).

columns.name: FIRST_SETTLE_DATE

columns.name: FIX_TO_FLOAT_COUPON_FREQ

columns.name: FIXED_CRRNCY_IND

columns.name: FIXED_IND

columns.name: FIXING_DATE
columns.comment: The fixing date for non-deliverable forward contracts.

columns.name: FLOAT_PAY_DATE
columns.comment: For unadjusted coupon conventions (FL141, FLT_CPN_CONVENTION), the pay day is the coupon pay date. For Following Bus Day - Adjusted, it is the initial pay day. The possible pay definitions are:    Calendar day: 1-31    3rd Wednesday of month    1st Wednesday of month    1st business day    Last business day    At maturity    Irreg. Cpn (Mex Dom FRN)    1st Monday    Last Day of month    Odd Cpn Frequencies    1st Thursday of month    Last Bus Day No Leap Yr.

columns.name: FRANKED_IND
columns.comment: Indicator to show if Security is franked. Understood to mean that the company pays dividends that do not incur tax for the payee.

columns.name: FRST_EXERCISE_DATE
columns.comment: First date that option can be exercised from.

columns.name: FTF_TRANSITION_DATE
columns.comment: Date on which a Fix to Float security switches from fix rate coupons to floating rate coupons.

columns.name: FUND_ASSET_CLASS_FOCUS
columns.comment: Broad asset class that the fund intends to invest in. An asset class is a grouping of investments that exhibit similar characteristics and are subject to the same laws and regulations. This focus is interpreted from the fund's prospectus.        Possible Values:        Equity; Fixed Income; Mixed Allocation; Money Market; Real Estate; Commodity; Specialty; Private Equity; Alternative.        The field returns the asset class focus as defined by the fund company. Holdings Based Asset Class Focus (FD326, HB_ASSET_CLASS_FOCUS) returns the asset class focus calculated based off of the reported portfolio holdings of the fund.

columns.name: FUND_GEOGRAPHIC_FOCUS
columns.comment: Geographic area of focus the fund intends to invest in as stated in the prospectus. The classification selections include region, country and state.

columns.name: FUT_DELIV_FIRST_DATE
columns.comment: First delivery date of future product.

columns.name: FUT_EXCH_PROD_CD
columns.comment: Reference code representing futures product associated with the list exchange. Code details are available in the corresponding source system.

columns.name: FUT_LAST_TRADE_DATE
columns.comment: Last day of trading of future product.

columns.name: FUT_NOTICE_FIRST_DATE
columns.comment: The first day on which a notice of intent to deliver can be made by the clearinghouse to a buyer

columns.name: FUTURE_DELIVERABLE_BOND_ISIN
columns.comment: The ISIN numbers of the deliverable bonds for a future and their conversion factors.

columns.name: FUTURE_DELIVERY_LAST_DATE
columns.comment: The last date on which the underlying may be delivered into a futures contract.

columns.name: FUTURE_EQUIVALENT_RISK
columns.comment: The price sensitivity of the future contract to changes in yield on a semi-annual bond equivalent basis.

columns.name: FUTURE_IND
columns.comment: Future Indicator

columns.name: FUTURE_TYPE
columns.comment: The future type code. Code defined in DIM_CODE_VALUE as DESC_CD where DESC_TYPE = 'FUTTYP'.

columns.name: FUTURES_CATEGORY
columns.comment: Futures Category Type

columns.name: GICS_INDUSTRY_GROUP_NAME
columns.comment: A text description indicating GICS industry group classification.  GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) is an industry classification standard developed by MSCI in collaboration with Standard & Poors (S&P).  The Global Industry Classification Standard consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 62 industries, and 132 sub-industries. The GICS classification assigns an industry group name to each company according to its principal business activity.        For  Corps/Pfds: GICS data is retrieved for the Company ID (ID035, ID_BB_COMPANY) associated with the security.

columns.name: GICS_INDUSTRY_NAME
columns.comment: A text description indicating GICS industry classification. GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) is an industry classification standard developed by MSCI in collaboration with Standard & Poors (S&P).  The Global Industry Classification Standard consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 62 industries, and 132 sub-industries. The GICS classification assigns an industry name to each company according to its principal business activity.        For  Corps/Pfds: GICS data is retrieved for the Company ID (ID035, ID_BB_COMPANY) associated with the security.

columns.name: GICS_SECTOR_NAME
columns.comment: A text description indicating GICS sector classification. GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) is an industry classification standard developed by MSCI in collaboration with Standard & Poors (S&P).  The Global Industry Classification Standard consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 62 industries, and 132 sub-industries. The GICS classification assigns a sector name to each company according to its principal business activity.        For  Corps/Pfds: GICS data is retrieved for the Company ID (ID035, ID_BB_COMPANY) associated with the security.

columns.name: GICS_SUB_INDUSTRY_NAME
columns.comment: A text description indicating GICS sub-industry classification. GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) is an industry classification standard developed by MSCI in collaboration with Standard & Poors (S&P).  The Global Industry Classification Standard consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 68 industries, and 154 sub-industries. The GICS classification assigns a sub-industry name to each company according to its principal business activity.        For  Corps/Pfds: GICS data is retrieved for the Company ID (ID035, ID_BB_COMPANY) associated with the security.

columns.name: GUARANTOR_TYPE
columns.comment: Type of the Guarantors

columns.name: HIGHLY_PREDICTABLE_IND
columns.comment: Highly Predictable (HP) flag for LGAS Prepayable Securitised Bonds. A Highly predictable (HP) asset flag/attribute is to be assigned specifically for HP assets invested, to enable IR to report back IR HP limits to the PRA.

columns.name: HY_INDEX_FLAG
columns.comment: Security UDF Text 44. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR44

columns.name: HYBRID_IND
columns.comment:
Indicates bonds with qualities of both an interest bearing security (debt) and equity. Field will return "Y" for securities that are able to defer interest payments without defaulting. Deferred interest can be cumulative or non-cumulative, and may be conditional.

This field is related to Hybrid Cumulative Indicator (DZ294, HYBRID_CUMULATIVE_INDICATOR).

columns.name: IDX_SERIES
columns.comment: Covers Developed and Emerging markets and is suitable as the basis for investment products, such as funds, derivatives and exchange-traded funds.

columns.name: IDX_TERM
columns.comment: The code for maturity (tenor) or term of the Index.

columns.name: IDX_VERSION
columns.comment: Keeps track of schema changes and provides users with access to data in altered columns that are contained in indexes.

columns.name: IMPLIED_BASE_RATE
columns.comment: The implied rate is an interest rate equal to the difference between the spot rate and the forward or futures rate. The implied rate gives investors a way to compare returns across investments.

columns.name: INCORP_CNTRY_CD
columns.comment: Country of incorporation.

columns.name: INCORP_CNTRY_ISO_2
columns.comment:
Two character INCORP ISO country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: INCORP_CNTRY_ISO_3
columns.comment:
Three character INCORP ISO country code.
Availability of the referential data for the code contingent on the data service supporting data delivery from the vendor/3rd party.

columns.name: INCORP_CNTRY_NAME
columns.comment: Country name of Incorparation

columns.name: INDEX_BITMASK
columns.comment: Security UDF Text 46. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR46

columns.name: INDEX_DESK_ASSET_UOI
columns.comment: Index Desk Asset

columns.name: INDEX_FLAG_US_AGG
columns.comment: Security UDF Text 43. Mapped from DIM_SECURITY_UDF_STR.UDF_CHAR43

columns.name: INDEX_TYPE
columns.comment: The type of index.

columns.name: INDUSTRY_GROUP
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System)  classification based on the business or economic function of the party and its characteristics.
These Bloomberg mnemonics are represented in the hierarchy.
INDUSTRY_SECTOR = INDUSTRY level 1
INDUSTRY_GROUP = INDUSTRY level 2
INDUSTRY_SUBGROUP = INDUSTRY level 3

columns.name: INDUSTRY_GROUP_CD
columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System)  code classification based on the business or economic function of the party and its characteristics.
These Bloomberg mnemonics are represented in the hierarchy.
INDUSTRY_SECTOR = INDUSTRY level 1
INDUSTRY_GROUP = INDUSTRY level 2
INDUSTRY_SUBGROUP = INDUSTRY level 3

columns.comment:
BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System)  classification based on the business or economic function of the party and its characteristics.

INDUSTRY_SECTOR = INDUSTRY level 1

columns.comment:

INDUSTRY_SECTOR = INDUSTRY level 1

BICS (Bloomberg Industry Classification System)  classification based on the business or economic function of the party and its characteristics.
These Bloomberg mnemonics are represented in the hierarchy.
INDUSTRY_SECTOR = INDUSTRY level 1
INDUSTRY_GROUP = INDUSTRY level 2
